https://www.schumer.senate.gov/newsroom/: New York, N.Y. – U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today released the following statement on the denial of a permit to test howitzer cannons near the Taylor Pond Wild Forest and Jay Mountain Wilderness: “I applaud the Adirondack Park Agency Board and its staff for denying the proposal to create a howitzer testing range inside the Adirondack Park in Essex County. This kind of military testing operation should be done at another established firing range where our trained service members can conduct this testing safely and with regard for the environment and community. Firing a howitzer cannon on private land inside our treasured Adirondack Park is unacceptable and incongruous with the spirit of the ‘forever wild’ status the Adirondack Park is afforded by the state constitution.” ###

Schumer Says The Cost of Everything On The Thanksgiving Menu Has Skyrocketed Due to Trump’s Disastrous Policies, Reckless Tariffs, And Economic Uncertainty While Food Banks Are Scrambling To Keep Up With Surge In Demand North Country County Budgets Face $3.5+ MILLION Shortfall Next Year– And Up To $8.2 MILLION In Jefferson County Over The Next Two Years – Of Funding Needed To Help 48,000 North Country Residents Put Food On The Table Schumer To NY House Republicans: Help Families And Farmers – Stand Up Against Trump’s SNAP Cuts! After the Trump Administration’s devastating SNAP cuts—passed last year in the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill—took effect earlier this year, shifting greater costs onto New York counties and increasing hunger among the most vulnerable, and with Thanksgiving just three days away, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today stood alongside a bipartisan coalition of public officials, food system leaders, and community partners at Jefferson Community College’s Food Pantry to push to preserve nutrition assistance programs, delay the SNAP cost shift, and protect North Country taxpayers. In New York, counties administer the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), meaning $3.5 million in new annual costs have fallen directly on county budgets in the North Country, forcing communities to choose between raising local taxes or cutting food assistance for families, seniors, veterans, and others in need. In Jefferson County, taxpayers are on the hook for millions in new SNAP spending, which county officials report could cost as much as $8.2 million by the end of 2028. Over the next two years, Jefferson County is planning to budget $2.5 million to pay for the SNAP administrative cost shift, and as much as $5.7 million to cover the SNAP error rate cost shift. These cuts are hitting the North Country hard as families are preparing their Thanksgiving meals while costs for Thanksgiving staples have increased 11% compared to last year. With the administrative cost shift already straining county budgets, Schumer urged New York House Republicans to work with Democrats to enact a two-year delay to the SNAP cost shift and meet the needs of families across the country suffering from rising costs, reckless tariffs, and constant economic uncertainty. “48,000 New Yorkers across the North Country depend on SNAP to put food on the table. But last year, Trump made the largest cut to SNAP in history and is now forcing North Country taxpayers to pick up the tab,” said Senator Schumer. “Thanksgiving is just three days away, and these cuts are being implemented while the cost of everything on the menu has skyrocketed, and families don’t know where to turn. Trump’s bill has blown a $1 million hole in the Jefferson County budget, and counties across the state are being forced to choose between raising local taxes and cutting food assistance for hungry kids, seniors, veterans, and families. It’s just plain cruel.” Schumer added, “That’s why I’m here today: to demand that New York House Republicans stand with Democrats to reverse Trump’s cuts to SNAP and delay the cost shift. As we prepare to gather with our loved ones for Thanksgiving, I urge Republicans to come back to the table and work with Democrats to find bipartisan solutions that will help hardworking families who rely on these programs and ensure the tens of millions of Americans across the country who rely on food assistance have enough to eat.” The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) is the largest anti-hunger program in the United States and a lifeline for nearly 3 million NY children, seniors, veterans, and families who depend on this critical funding to purchase groceries. Last year, Trump and Congressional Republicans rushed to pass a nearly $200 billion cut to SNAP, ripping away food from thousands of hungry kids and families across America. Since the cuts were passed, 6 million Americans have lost access to SNAP, including more than 272,000 across New York State. New data from Hunger Free America (HFA) shows more than one-third (36%) of Americans struggled with food insecurity in 2026, more than double USDA’s 2024 estimate of 14%. Even more shocking, the survey found 41% of kids live in a food-insecure household, more than triple USDA’s 2021 estimate. The challenge of fitting groceries into a family’s budget doesn’t just hit the lowest income bracket; HFA found that nearly 20% of households with an annual income of more than $150,000 struggle to afford food. 77% of Americans worry about whether food banks will have enough food to meet the current spike in demand, according to Feeding America. According to the 2026 North Country Adult Community Health Survey, more than one-in-five North Country residents reported eating less or skipping meals in the last year because they did not have enough money for food. Demand across the Food Bank of Central New York’s North Country food network surged by nearly 34%, or 1,600 individuals, from July to October, and last month the network served more than 6,500 people in Jefferson, St. Lawrence, and Lewis Counties. At Jefferson Community College’s Food Pantry, weekly visits have risen about 85% year over year, and with five weeks remaining in 2026, the pantry has already served 60% more visitors than it did in all of 2025. Since SNAP is administered by counties in New York, they are being forced to shoulder the burden of increased SNAP costs, using more local dollars to administer the program because less federal funding is available. During recessions or economic downturns, these impacts will be even more acute, as more people apply for benefits and state revenue declines; more children, seniors, veterans, people with disabilities, and others will not be able to access this vital program due to insufficient funding. In addition, earlier this month, the Trump administration proposed a new rule that would restrict more than 5.5 million additional Americans from receiving SNAP benefits. As Congress approaches the end of the year and these cuts are implemented with the holiday season upon us, high costs are hitting New York families especially hard as they prepare for their Thanksgiving dinners. According to a new report from Groundwork Collaborative, Thanksgiving costs have increased by 11% compared to last year: a frozen turkey has increased 26%, candied yams are up over 10%, and green beans are up a whopping 36%. Schumer said it is more important than ever for Democrats and Republicans to find bipartisan solutions to what is shaping up to be an American hunger crisis not seen in generations. There have been strong bipartisan calls to reverse course and support the SNAP cost shift delay from governors, mayors, and state legislatures. Schumer is calling on New York House Republicans to join in the fight against these cruel food assistance cuts. “SNAP is a federal program that should be funded with federal dollars. If there is no change or delay to the SNAP cost shift, over the next two years Jefferson County is looking at $2.5 million in new administrative costs and up to $5.7 million in new expenses to cover the SNAP error rate,” said Jefferson County Administrator Ryan Piche. “On behalf of Jefferson County and the community we serve, I would like to thank Senator Schumer for convening this bipartisan coalition of North Country leaders to fight for a delay in this unfunded SNAP mandate before it crowds out essential local services and costs our taxpayers millions.” "This is not a one-time cost. Shifting more than $1.8 million a year in SNAP administration onto Jefferson and St. Lawrence Counties left local leaders with the decision to raise the levy above the tax cap to cover a cost like this; that increase becomes part of the base and carries forward every year after. Property taxpayers in the North Country will feel this for years to come,” said New York State Assemblyman Scott Gray . “Our counties did what they had to do to keep services running for more than 25,000 neighbors who rely on SNAP. Washington needs to delay implementation and work with Albany to fix the error rate calculation. Property taxpayers are left holding the bill, which doesn't result in savings to anyone. I would like to thank Senator Schumer for leading the charge in Congress to pass a multi-year delay and working across the aisle to protect taxpayers and feed families here in the North Country.” “As winter approaches in the North Country, families continue to struggle to put food on their tables, keep the lights on and the home heated. Continued disruptions in SNAP have ripple effects across our food system, let alone the financial hardships placed on families. Food pantries have seen an increased demand month to month, some as high as 25%. Now, the administrative cost shifts will hit our counties even more,” said Adirondack Food Systems Network Director Joshua Stephani . “That fact is simple: no program, no agency, and no organization can replace the effectiveness of SNAP in bringing people and families out of poverty. AFSN thanks Senator Schumer for his continued fight to support our families in the North Country through the protection of SNAP cuts and delaying cost shifts in our counties." “SNAP matters to our schools in ways people don't always see. Nearly two-thirds of students in our district qualify for free or reduced-price meals, and more than half are automatically certified because their families receive SNAP or Medicaid. When families in our district lose their SNAP benefits, fewer students are certified and the cost of feeding them shifts to state taxpayers and local budgets. SNAP is also used to calculate the funding public schools receive to support students living in poverty. If those students and families are forced off SNAP by new rules or paperwork, our district could lose funding at exactly the moment our students need it most,” said Watertown Central School District Superintendent Dr. Larry Schmiegal . “This reaches beyond our school doors. SNAP brings about $32 million a year into Jefferson County, spent at local grocery stores and farm stands. SNAP dollars help our district cafeteria purchase thousands of pounds of fresh apples, thousands of ears of fresh corn, and even ground beef from local farms. Our county leaders have asked for more time to implement recent changes to the SNAP program, and I agree with them. On behalf of Watertown Central School District, I would like to thank Senator Schumer for convening this bipartisan coalition of federal, state and local partners to fight for our SNAP benefits, and for leading the charge in Congress to pass a multi-year delay so that schools and communities have time to plan a transition that doesn't leave students behind.” According to a report from the New York State Association of Counties, 13,184 New Yorkers in Jefferson County receive $32 million in annual benefits through SNAP. The planned cost shift is expected to leave Jefferson County with at least $1,052,497 in annual budget costs, at the same time as the county is already managing state and federal mandates, workforce shortages, rising service demands, and the property tax cap. Across the North Country, more than 48,000 New Yorkers receive $115 million in annual SNAP benefits. The cost shift will transfer more than $3.5 million in costs to counties in the North Country. The 2027 Jefferson County budget said that cost shifts from the federal level, especially from the “Big, Beautiful Bill,” are creating unprecedented pressure on county expenditures. After Nearly Two Years Of Plummeting Tourism, Skyrocketing Costs, And Small Businesses Paying The Price For Harmful Trade Policies, Schumer Says Northern NY Is On The Front Lines Of The Trade War And Tariffs Must End Now Schumer’s New Bill – The End Trump’s Tariff Tax Act – Would Terminate Trump’s Latest Round Of Global And 50% Canadian Tariffs To Deliver Lower Costs For Families, Seniors, & Small Businesses Schumer To Trump: Dump These Damaging Tariffs To Lower Costs Or I Will With Trump’s tariffs driving nearly two straight years of declining tourism and skyrocketing costs, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today stood in Massena with a bipartisan coalition of Northern New York business owners, public officials, and concerned community members being crushed by Trump’s tariff war to announce his new legislation – the End Trump’s Tariff Tax Act – to revoke Trump’s most recent tariffs, including 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. Schumer said that as Trump makes threats to annex Canada and rename Lake Ontario, costs for families and local businesses are skyrocketing. The senator said his bill is key to reversing the damage done by Trump’s tariff taxes, stopping this nonsensical trade war, and lowering costs for Upstate New York’s families and small businesses. Schumer vowed quick action in the new Congress to provide relief by curtailing Trump’s chaotic trade war and the constant economic uncertainty. “Costs are skyrocketing, small businesses are being squeezed, and family farms are getting hammered because of Trump’s tariff taxes and costly trade war. That’s why I’m here announcing my bill to immediately end this tariff war and bring down costs. Because instead of making life more affordable for hardworking families, Trump is focused on directing taxpayer dollars to his billionaire friends, doubling down on his misguided effort to rename New York’s beloved Lake Ontario, and threatening to make Canada the 51 st state,” said Senator Schumer. “In Northern New York, small businesses are struggling because of rising costs that are slowing growth and squeezing margins. It’s a gut punch to North Country businesses, to New York’s economy, and to American families that are being hit hard by Trump’s tariff temper tantrums. In January, one of my very first actions will be to end Trump’s tariff taxes on New York’s families and businesses.” In July, Trump levied 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods, including products that had previously been protected by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) that Trump himself negotiated and signed during his first term. Schumer said this follows a series of unnecessary provocations directed toward our closest trading partner, ally, and neighbor to the north, Canada. Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario ‘Lake America’ and has repeatedly threatened to make Canada its 51 st state. As a result of Trump’s escalating tariff war, Canadians are canceling trips to the United States , and tourism has declined across all the major bridge ports of entry between New York and Canada compared to 2024. Curran Renewable Energy, a family-owned logging business that has operated in Massena since 1976, has been quoted markups as high as 50% and has faced hundreds of thousands in additional costs caused by tariffs. Over the past year, Curran was forced to pay a tariff-driven markup of $100,000 for a new log washer, and the company postponed plans to acquire new trailers for its shipping fleet because tariffs increased the total cost of the purchase by as much as $500,000. Curran would like to increase pay to help their employees deal with higher prices, but they have not been able to because tariffs are increasing business expenses and squeezing margins. The Ogdensburg Bridge & Port Authority , located along the St. Lawrence River directly across from Canada, has dealt with a significant downtick in traffic at the Ogdensburg International Airport, Ogdensburg Prescott International Bridge, and the Port of Ogdensburg. In 2025, decreased cross-border traffic resulted in a 34.9 percent decrease in tolls and over $500,000 in lost revenue. This year, the OBPA is closing in on nearly $1,000,000 in lost revenue as a result of tariffs. Port leadership reports that tariff-driven uncertainty has caused companies it does business with to postpone large decisions or cancel plans outright. Twin Mill Farms , a family-owned dairy and crop farm spanning more than 1,000 acres in Lisbon, milks around 400 to 550 Holstein cows and grows cash crops like corn, soybeans, and more. As a farm on the northern border, Twin Mill has been on the front lines of the trade war with Canada and felt the bite of tariffs in real time. As tariffs drive up costs for farms and agricultural businesses, Twin Mill reports significant markups caused by tariffs on everything from farm equipment and replacement parts to fertilizer and fuel. At the same time, retaliatory tariffs and trade actions aimed at American markets are driving down demand and prices for Twin Mill and dairy farms across the North Country. Simplicity , a boutique retailer located in downtown Massena, sources many of its products from small brands and wholesalers, so a significant portion of its sales originate overseas. As a result, when tariffs go up, the boutique’s wholesale costs go up with them. Like many small businesses, Simplicity cannot absorb tariff costs like big chains can, forcing the business to either pass higher costs on to customers or continue getting squeezed at the margin. Either way, tariffs have made it harder for Simplicity to keep the doors open, keep the boutique’s three employees working, and keep prices fair for local patrons. “The United States, New York State, and the North Country region have built a fully integrated economy and relationship with our Canadian friends and neighbors just across the river. For decades we have been making things together and sharing resources,” said Ben Dixon, Executive Director of the St. Lawrence County Chamber of Commerce . “In this productive and non-traditional relationship, the vitality of our businesses and communities grows strongest together, when we have a healthy exchange of tourism, material goods, energy, and commerce. Accordingly, we have continued to aggressively market our region to our Canadian neighbors with a truly sincere message that we welcome and appreciate them and want to continue to grow together.” Schumer declared it is time to put an end to Trump’s trade war with Canada that is hurting communities across America and raising costs for working families. Schumer said Americans are paying the price for Trump’s policies and being crushed by rising costs caused by Trump’s tariff taxes and costly trade war. Data released last month found that families have had to spend an additional $6,000 on everyday essentials under Trump due to rising prices for housing, groceries, gas, electricity, healthcare, and more. Schumer’s End Trump’s Tariff Tax Act would revoke President Trump’s latest barrage of tariffs and repeal the archaic authorities he has used to continue his trade war. This legislation would apply to President Trump’s recent Section 301 tariffs on 60 countries, previously imposed Section 122 temporary global tariffs, and the 50% Canadian tariffs. Schumer continues to be one of the leading advocates in Congress to end this unnecessary, ill-conceived, and damaging trade war with Canada that is decimating Upstate NY’s economy, tourism, small businesses, and local jobs. Last year, Schumer twice used a special fast-track process to force a vote in the Senate to end Trump’s destructive trade war with Canada. Businesses across Upstate New York are feeling renewed pain because of the Trump Administration’s latest barrage of tariffs. Last month, Schumer stood with a bipartisan coalition of businesses and community partners at the Port of Oswego to call for an end to the trade war and tariffs: The Port of Oswego Authority, located on the shores of Lake Ontario directly across from Canada, has been hit especially hard, losing upwards of $1 million in potential revenue as a result of the administration’s tariffs and trade war. The port is worried that if the tariffs and trade war continue, it will make it increasingly difficult to invest in the infrastructure needed to be prepared for an influx of demand on Central NY’s horizon with Micron and other new manufacturing investments underway across the region. Eagle Metalcraft , a multi-generational metal fabricator located in Syracuse, has lost millions of dollars as a result of tariffs. Though the administration claims its tariffs will bring new businesses into the United States, Eagle Metalcraft reports that the opposite is happening to its business. Eagle Metalcraft said that it lost 50% of revenue from one of its primary customers, who moved manufacturing and much of its purchasing to Asia to avoid the impact of tariffs, and was forced to go through two rounds of layoffs and part ways with six employees. Sterling House Farm , a small, multi-generational family farm with land in Cayuga and St. Lawrence Counties, has felt the pain of rising costs and uncertainty caused by tariffs on lumber, equipment, and fertilizer both personally and across their community. In order to complete a new greenhouse in Sterling, the farm had to move its business from local lumber yards like Ace Hardware in Oswego to specialty mills to avoid surging prices caused by tariffs, turning what was expected to be a one-season build into a multi-year endeavor that ran thousands of dollars over budget. 114 Reserve , a small café and community hub located in Fulton, is paying $1 more per pound for coffee beans and nearly 50% more for heavy whipping cream and oat milk, as well as significant markups on syrup, cocoa, electricity, and paper products driven by tariffs and the trade war with Canada. With customers already facing increased costs on everything from their gasoline to their grocery store bill, 114 Reserve has been unable to raise prices, which has led to shrinking margins, thousands of dollars in lost profit, and prevented the hiring of new staff. "On behalf of the Port of Oswego and community we serve, I would like to thank Senator Schumer for his leadership in fighting back against the negative effects that this administration’s tariffs on Canada are having on the port, our customers, local workers, and the Central New York economy,” said Port of Oswego Executive Director Tom Drumm . “The harmful and unnecessary trade war caused by these tariffs directly hampers the port’s ability to carry out its core business, translating into more than $1 million of lost potential revenue, increased volatility in demand and order flow, and fewer hours for our best in class maritime workforce. It has also frustrated the port’s plans for the growth and modernization needed to support Central NY’s ongoing manufacturing renaissance. I am proud to stand with Senator Schumer and the bipartisan coalition he assembled on our docks to push for passage of federal legislation that will end the trade war with Canada, stabilize costs, and protect working families.” Last year, Schumer stood at 1812 on the River in Sackett’s Harbor to push for an end to the administration’s sweeping International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariffs – which were ultimately found to be unconstitutional by the U.S. Supreme Court – alongside small businesses from across the region, including: 1812 Brewing Company in Watertown had its award-winning, American-made craft beer ripped off Ontario shelves in response to tariffs on Canada, slashing 10-15% of the company’s total business overnight, decreasing the company’s 2025 sales by at least $100,000 in 2025, and undoing years of hard work and investment to break into the Canadian market. Apothecary Chocolates in Colton was forced to close its doors and lay off three full-time employees after tariffs surged the price of a bag of its specialty chocolate by more than 180% – from $125 in 2024 to over $350 as of August 2025. Monthly Boxer in Watertown has faced a significant downtick in customer volume, order flow, and total revenue, which the company attributes directly to tariff rates and their volatility. The company says customers are downsizing, delaying, and even cancelling orders because of tariff-driven uncertainty in pricing and demand. Lake & River Roasters in Cape Vincent has watched adversarial rhetoric and trade policies aimed at Canada and other key trading partners drive away friends, family, and repeat customers from across the border, as tariffs have doubled the average price of their imported coffee beans – from around $3 per pound to $6 or more – in less than one year. This has forced the company to either charge more for impacted products at the risk of pricing out customers or absorb the added costs at the risk of operating on unsustainable margins. With every economic data point flashing red because of Trump’s chaotic trade war, Schumer called on Republicans to stand up for Upstate NY businesses and working families. Schumer said ending this costly trade war is key to protecting American families from price increases and job losses. ###

Schumer Says Federal Legislation Is Needed To Provide Relief From Rising Costs & Restore Certainty For Manufacturers The Raymond Corporation Is One Of Chenango County’s Largest Employers, Supporting 2,000+ Good-Paying Jobs Locally Schumer: Lift Tariffs To Lower Costs Today, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer visited The Raymond Corporation in Greene, NY. Since 1922, The Raymond Corporation, a member of the Toyota Industries family of companies, has been headquartered in Chenango County. Raymond has established itself as a global provider of industry-leading lift trucks and cutting-edge energy solutions. During the visit, Senator Schumer discussed challenges impacting the company, including tariffs, trade policy uncertainty, and workforce development. The senator also discussed with the company’s leadership opportunities to strengthen and expand domestic manufacturing. “For over 100 years, Raymond has been at the forefront of innovation, establishing itself as a global leader. Now, the company powers the region’s economy and supports over 2,000 good-paying jobs in Greene,” said Senator Schumer. “In January, one of my very first actions as the next Senate Majority Leader will be to lift these costly tariffs, lower costs, and end the trade war. Raymond develops and manufactures technology that makes trade possible—the double-faced wooden pallet and hydraulic hand pallet truck were even patented here—and I promise to keep working to help the company reach new heights.” The Raymond Corporation currently spans five U.S.-based manufacturing and energy facilities. Across New York, the company employs people in Greene, Kirkwood, Syracuse, and Rochester, supporting over 2,500 good-paying jobs. Raymond develops and manufactures lift trucks, including electric forklifts, pallet trucks, and hand pallet jacks. “We appreciate Senator Schumer’s visit and the opportunity to showcase Raymond’s longstanding commitment to American manufacturing. As a global organization, we support fair trade policies that facilitate the movement of materials, components, and finished product across international borders. Predictable and balanced trade policies are essential to maintaining competitiveness, strengthening supply chains, and supporting continued investment and job creation in the U.S.,” said Michael Field, COO of TMHNA. For years, Schumer has traveled across New York, hearing from manufacturers , breweries , and small business owners . Schumer said the message in every region is the same: the tariff taxes and costly trade war are slowing growth and squeezing margins. In September, Schumer introduced the End Trump’s Tariff Tax Act , which would revoke the latest barrage of tariffs and repeal authorities used to conduct the trade war. This legislation would apply to the administration’s recent Section 301 tariffs on 60 countries, previously imposed Section 122 temporary global tariffs, and the 50% Canadian tariffs. “The Raymond Corporation is a major employer and longstanding partner in the Southern Tier. Over the years, its continued growth and investment reflect the strength of the Southern Tier as a hub for manufacturing. However, like many businesses of all sizes across the region, rising costs from tariffs and the trade war are creating uncertainty. The region’s business community appreciates Senator Schumer’s efforts to lower costs, provide greater certainty, and support the businesses that power our economy,” said Stacey Duncan, CEO of the Leadership Alliance . Despite rising costs and growing uncertainty, Raymond has continued to invest in New York. In 2024, following Schumer’s efforts to transform the Southern Tier and Finger Lakes into a national hub for battery research and manufacturing, Raymond and Toyota Material Handling North America (TMHNA) invested $15 million to establish a new Energy Solutions Manufacturing Center of Excellence in Kirkwood, creating up to 45 new jobs . The company also opened a new advanced energy storage solutions development, prototyping, and test center in Henrietta, creating up to 40 new jobs . This center supports collaboration with energy storage resources in Rochester to support its energy solutions technology, including lithium-ion batteries and fuel cells. Schumer added, “Raymond’s commitment to New York is clear, and I look forward to leading the charge to remove barriers to their growth, create new opportunities for expansion, and ensure they can continue to invest in their top-notch workforce.” In 2022, Schumer delivered $63.7 million in federal funding for Binghamton University’s New Energy New York proposal to make the Southern Tier and Finger Lakes a national hub for battery research and manufacturing. In 2023, Schumer secured the prestigious Tech Hubs designation , a program Schumer created in his bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law, for Binghamton University’s New Energy New York (NENY) project. In 2024, Schumer announced the Binghamton University-led Upstate New York Energy Storage Engine won the esteemed U.S. National Science Foundation’s Regional “Innovation Engines” Competition (NSF Engines) , which was created by his CHIPS & Science Law, bringing $15 million in federal funding immediately, with the possibility of up to $160 million total over the entirety of the program. In 2026, Schumer announced that the Upstate New York Energy Storage Engine was selected as an awardee for the second phase of the NSF Engines Program , bringing up to $45 million over the next 3 years for Binghamton’s battery hub. ###

Earlier This Year, Lawmakers Urged U.S. Customs And Border Protection And The U.S. General Services Administration To Halt Plans To Build A Detention Center In Federal Building, Citing Disruptions To Federal Court, A Childcare Facility, & Other Critical Services Lawmakers Warn Trump Admin Against Moving To Another Facility In Rochester Area & Say Agency Must Be Transparent With Local Officials And Community Members About Any Future Plans In The Region Schumer, Gillibrand, Morelle: No Detention Facilities In Rochester Following their opposition to the Trump administration’s plan to build a Border Patrol detention center in downtown Rochester , U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, and U.S. Congressman Joseph Morelle today announced that U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), which oversees U.S. Border Patrol, has backed off its ill-conceived plan to build a detention center in the Kenneth B. Keating Federal Building. The General Services Administration (GSA), which runs the Keating Federal Building, has notified the Western District Federal Court that CBP has withdrawn its request for new space in the Keating Federal Building to assess other options. The lawmakers reiterated their staunch opposition to plans to expand existing or construct new U.S. Border Patrol detention facilities in the region and warned the Trump administration against trying to do so without the input of local leaders and community members. “I’m proud to announce that there will be no immigration detention center in downtown Rochester at the Keating Federal Building. Earlier this year, after the Trump administration’s Customs and Border Protection announced this absurd plan, with no communication with local officials, no public comment period, and no transparency. We demanded CBP stop the secrecy and back off this ill-conceived plan,” said Senator Schumer. “I applaud Rochester’s local leaders and the community members who joined our call, rallying at the federal building on a nearly weekly basis to push back against CBP’s unwelcome plans. I will always stand with Upstate New Yorkers to protect local communities from the Trump administration’s extreme plans to build or expand detention facilities, including expanding the detention center in Batavia. Border Patrol needs to be reined in and reformed from top to bottom – not expanded.” “Placing a 24/7 Customs and Border Protection detention center inside the Keating federal building – alongside a childcare facility and critical public services – was the wrong decision from day one. I am proud to have stood with Senator Schumer, Congressman Morelle, and local advocates to stop this plan in its tracks. While I am relieved CBP has withdrawn its request, the Trump administration must not attempt to quietly relocate this facility elsewhere in the Rochester area without full transparency and input from local officials and residents,” said Senator Kirsten Gillibrand. “This is a major victory for the people of Rochester who made their voices heard and refused to accept the Trump Administration’s reckless plan to bring immigration detention cells into the heart of our downtown,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “I’m grateful to Senator Schumer and Senator Gillibrand for their partnership in fighting this proposal, and I will continue fighting to protect our community from Donald Trump’s cruel immigration agenda.” In March, the lawmakers in a letter to the CBP Commissioner and the Acting Administrator of the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) explained that building a detention center would disrupt the day-to-day operations of other federal offices in the building and the Western District of New York Federal Courts. The lawmakers emphasized opposition to this plan from local residents and officials, the legal community , and more, and demanded clarity and transparency from the Trump administration. ###

Five Years Ago, Then-GlobalFoundries CEO Tom Caulfield Said That If Schumer Could Create Federal Incentives For Semiconductor Manufacturing, GlobalFoundries Would Build A Second Fab – Today, Schumer Says A Promise Made Is A Promise Kept Powered By Billions In Funding From Schumer’s Bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law, GlobalFoundries Is Breaking Ground On New, Second Manufacturing Facility That Will Create Thousands Of Good-Paying Jobs In Capital Region Schumer: GlobalFoundries’ Groundbreaking Marks Next Chapter In American Chipmaking After years of work to rebuild semiconductor manufacturing in New York and America through his CHIPS & Science Law, including working relentlessly with GlobalFoundries to support expansion of their New York operations, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today celebrated GlobalFoundries’ historic groundbreaking for its second, state-of-the-art fab in Malta, NY. Thanks to billions from Schumer’s CHIPS & Science Law, this expansion will create thousands of good-paying manufacturing and union construction jobs in the Capital Region. “What is the only thing better than one economy-changing, job-creating chip fab? Two chip fabs! Powered by billions in federal investment, shovels are hitting the ground for GlobalFoundries’ second, state-of-the-art chip fab in Malta! Today is a historic day for Saratoga County and Upstate New York as we usher in the next chapter of the country’s hi-tech manufacturing future,” said Senator Schumer. “When I visited Malta to push for my groundbreaking CHIPS & Science Law, GlobalFoundries said that if Congress created federal incentives for semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries would build a second fab. We both took our promises seriously, and now here we are, bringing thousands of good-paying manufacturing and union construction jobs to the Capital Region. I’m proud to have delivered billions in federal CHIPS funding to GlobalFoundries to make this day possible and to bring this second fab and thousands of good jobs to life. America’s next era of chip manufacturing is underway here in Upstate, and I can confidently say New York’s best days are ahead.” Schumer said this transformational investment was just what he had envisioned when he helped write and pass into law the bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law. Schumer has worked for years to expand GlobalFoundries’ New York presence, with a focus on delivering a second fab. SCHUMER’S LANDMARK BIPARTISAN CHIPS & SCIENCE LAW For years, Schumer has been a staunch advocate for securing the domestic semiconductor and microelectronic supply chain and making historic investments in manufacturing and innovation. After decades of Upstate NY losing manufacturing, Schumer has prioritized bringing manufacturing back to Upstate NY, with a focus on positioning the state to lead in fast-growing, critical industries like semiconductor manufacturing. In May 2020, Schumer unveiled the Endless Frontier Act with bipartisan support to build on U.S. science and technology leadership through investments in research and development and strengthening regional economic development, manufacturing, and supply chains. After a year of negotiation, in June 2021, Schumer announced Senate passage of the U.S. Competition and Innovation Act , which combined his Endless Frontier Act and major new federal funding for federal incentives to bring semiconductor manufacturing back to the U.S., including dedicated support for chip production, like that of GlobalFoundries, that is essential to the auto industry, the military, and other critical industries. When Schumer visited GlobalFoundries’ Malta campus in July 2021 to tout efforts on the federal level to invest in the domestic semiconductor industry, then-CEO Tom Caulfield told Schumer that if Congress successfully created federal incentives for semiconductor manufacturing and research and development, GlobalFoundries would build a second fab. Motivated by the prospect of new investments like a second fab in the Capital Region and strengthening of our national security by expanding this critical industry in America, Schumer worked tirelessly to craft and pass the CHIPS & Science Law with bipartisan support. After years of work, Schumer led the CHIPS & Science Law to passage with bipartisan support in the Senate in August 2022, creating major federal investment for new domestic manufacturing in the Capital Region, Upstate New York, and across the country. Four years after his landmark CHIPS & Science Act was signed into law, Upstate New York is now powering the nation’s semiconductor comeback, attracting billions of dollars of investment, and delivering tens of thousands of new, good-paying jobs across Upstate NY. DELIVERING FEDERAL INVESTMENT FOR GLOBALFOUNDRIES Since Schumer led his CHIPS & Science Law to passage, this landmark legislation has delivered billions in federal support for GlobalFoundries’ growth in the Capital Region. In February 2024, Schumer announced a $1.5 billion award for GlobalFoundries’ expansion in the Capital Region, including the second, state-of-the-art fab that is being unveiled today. The award was finalized in November 2024. The federal CHIPS Investment Tax Credit created by Schumer's CHIPS & Science Law is also providing a critical federal incentive to make this project possible. GlobalFoundries then secured an additional $75 million in CHIPS funding to make a $3 billion investment to create a first-of-its-kind advanced chip packaging facility at its Saratoga County location, thanks to Schumer’s CHIPS & Science Law. A few months ago, GlobalFoundries finalized an agreement for up to $375 million in CHIPS funding, made possible by Schumer’s CHIPS & Science Law, to launch Quantum Technology Solutions, a new quantum business within GlobalFoundries that will position America at the forefront of technology innovation. Earlier this summer, GlobalFoundries received a letter of intent from the Department of Commerce to award up to $300 million in CHIPS funding from Schumer’s CHIPS & Science Law for accelerating domestic silicon photonics research and development to support artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Together, these billions in CHIPS investments have and will continue to support GlobalFoundries’ growth, create thousands of good-paying manufacturing and union construction jobs, and support the Capital Region and Upstate New York’s growth as a global tech hub. In addition, GlobalFoundries has committed to a Project Labor Agreement, establishing employment terms and conditions with unions before workers are hired. GlobalFoundries is a leading producer of essential chips that are critical across industries, from mobile phones and artificial intelligence to automobiles and defense technologies. Currently, there are only four companies outside of China that provide current and mature foundry capabilities at the scale of GlobalFoundries, and GlobalFoundries is the only one of those companies that is headquartered in the United States. GlobalFoundries, a Trusted Foundry for the Department of Defense, is a key supplier of chips for America’s national defense, with strong partnerships with major defense contractors like Lockheed Martin. GlobalFoundries also supplies chips to America’s auto industry with partnerships in place with companies like General Motors, which saw severe shortages of chips during the pandemic, leading to increased prices for cars. The investment will support the expansion of GlobalFoundries’ current fab focused on automotive chips to help meet soaring demand for chips in cars and get ahead of future supply chain challenges. BUILDING UPSTATE NEW YORK’S MANUFACTURING ECOSYSTEM Thanks to Schumer’s CHIPS & Science Law, Upstate New York has seen a major revival in tech manufacturing. Schumer has worked for years to highlight the Capital Region and broader Upstate NY’s ability to lead the country’s semiconductor manufacturing efforts. In the Capital Region, beyond Schumer’s relentless advocacy for expansion of GlobalFoundries, he has also focused on positioning Albany NanoTech as a global leader in semiconductor research and development. Schumer brought former Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo to the Capital Region several times , including to GlobalFoundries and to meet with leaders of Albany NanoTech, to highlight the region’s ability to lead in semiconductor research and manufacturing. Schumer additionally convinced South Korea to establish chip research and development partnerships at Albany NanoTech. Thanks to Schumer’s advocacy, Albany NanoTech is now home to a major new IBM multi-billion-dollar quantum wafer fab investment, made possible by $1 billion in federal CHIPS R&D funding. Albany NanoTech will also feature a new $10 billion High NA EUV Lithography Center, made possible with a $1 billion investment from Governor Hochul and New York State. Albany NanoTech’s world-renowned capabilities were also central to Schumer and Governor Hochul’s successful effort to secure Micron’s massive $100+ billion megafab project in Upstate NY, with Micron saying Albany NanoTech was a critical factor in their selection of Central NY for their major investment to bring advanced memory chip manufacturing to the U.S. Earlier this year, Micron broke ground on a historic $100+ billion investment to build a cutting-edge memory fab in Central New York with the support of an over $6 billion CHIPS agreement. In addition, Corning Incorporated finalized a $32 million CHIPS funding agreement to make a $315 million investment that would increase production at its Canton facility of specialized glass vital for the semiconductor industry. Edwards Vacuum has officially opened a new first-of-its-kind-in-the-country $300+ million, 600-job dry pump manufacturing facility, supported by an $18 million CHIPS funding award. TTM Technologies, a printed circuit board manufacturer, has opened a major new facility expansion in Onondaga County, creating up to 400 good-paying jobs, supported by $30 million in federal investment that Schumer delivered. Schumer said GlobalFoundries’ growth was a key part of his vision for a thriving manufacturing hub in Upstate New York, and with these new investments thanks to his CHIPS & Science Law, new growth is coming to the region bigger and better than imagined. ###

New Grants Will Fund Local Safety Action Plans To Prevent Roadway Fatalities and Serious Injuries Senators Say Fed $$$ Funded Through Bipartisan Infrastructure Law They Championed Will Help Save Lives In Capital Region And Make For Safer Commutes Schumer, Gillibrand, Tonko: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Is Paving The Way For Safer Streets And Roads In Capital Region! U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, and U.S. Congressman Paul Tonko today announced $8,180,000 from the Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law in Safe Streets and Roads For All (SS4A) grant funding to improve safety at major roadways throughout the Capital Region. The lawmakers explained that this funding will fund safety analyses and launch pilot programs for emergency vehicle alerts, prehospital blood delivery, and more to improve roadway safety outcomes in Albany, Columbia, Fulton, Greene, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Saratoga, Schenectady, and Schoharie counties. “The Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law we passed is paving the way for safer roads in the Capital Region. I am proud to deliver this $8.2 million federal investment to help give communities across the Capital Region the tools they need to improve street safety,” said Senator Schumer. “These grants will help improve road safety and save lives by developing comprehensive action plans. I will continue fighting to deliver funding for safer streets in every corner of New York.” “Programs like Safe Streets and Roads for All are vital to preventing traffic tragedies in our communities,” said Senator Gillibrand. “This $8.2 million investment will allow the Capital Region to develop and implement targeted safety plans where they are needed most. I am proud to deliver these federal dollars, and I will keep fighting to ensure New Yorkers can travel safely.” “Before the investments made with our Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, our communities faced many hazards from crumbling road and water infrastructure, legacy pollution, and other serious threats to safety,” Congressman Tonko said . “Thanks to our historic law, we’re seeing meaningful action that makes our Capital Region a better, safer place to call home. I look forward to seeing our New York communities continue to reap the benefits of this investment, and pledge to not stop in my effort to deliver for our Capital Region and beyond.” The lawmakers explained that the nearly $8.2 million will be divided between three projects serving nine counties: $4 million for the Capital Region Integrated Roadway Safety and Post-Crash Care Initiative to develop a Supplemental Action Plan and conduct demonstration activities focused on post-crash care, emergency response coordination, and crash prevention across New York’s Capital Region. Work includes safety analysis, partner coordination, protocol development, and pilots for emergency vehicle alerts, responder data interoperability, prehospital blood delivery, and responder protection to improve survivability, dispatch efficiency, and roadway safety outcomes. $4 million for the Wilton Emergency Squad in Saratoga County to develop a Supplemental Action Plan and conduct demonstration activities focused on post-crash care, emergency response coordination, and roadway safety across its service area. Work includes safety analysis of high-risk corridors, stakeholder coordination, protocol development, and temporary pilots such as emergency vehicle transponder alerts, data interoperability tools, signal pre-emption, and prehospital blood delivery to inform future safety initiatives. $180,000 for the City of Hudson to develop its first Comprehensive Safety Action Plan for the city and conduct a temporary demonstration activity at a community-identified location. The work includes developing a high-injury network, completing a systemic risk assessment, reviewing policies, engaging partners and the public, and identifying safety strategies to address crashes involving vulnerable road users and freight traffic; demonstration results such as speed and near-miss data will inform the final Action Plan. The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which Schumer led to passage as Majority Leader, established the SS4A discretionary program with $5 billion in appropriated funds over 5 years, 2022-2026. The SS4A program funds regional, local, and Tribal initiatives through grants to prevent roadway deaths and serious injuries. The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law more than doubled funding for surface transportation programs that improve roadway safety. ###

Schumer Worked Tirelessly To Convince This Major Semiconductor Supply Chain Company To Build Its First American Factory In Upstate New York And Delivered $18 MILLION In Fed Support From His CHIPS & Science Law To Bring New Facility To Life Major Semiconductor Companies Need Advanced Vacuum Technology That Edwards Vacuum Will Make In The USA With Hardworking Western New York Workforce Schumer: Edwards Vacuum Is Ready To Pump Up Upstate New York’s Semiconductor Superhighway! After years of direct advocacy, urging Edwards Vacuum to invest in Western New York, and delivering an $18 million federal award from his bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law to support the new facility, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today celebrated the grand opening of the first dry pump manufacturing facility for the semiconductor industry to be located in the United States. Edwards Vacuum’s new facility in Genesee County is expected to have a $300+ million investment and create a whopping 600+ good-paying jobs when the facility reaches full production capacity. “Edwards Vacuum, America’s first semiconductor dry pump manufacturing facility, is open for business right here in Genesee County! Today, major semiconductor companies will now look to Genesee County as home to the advanced vacuum technology they need for their chip fabs that Edwards Vacuum will now make in the USA, bringing this critical high-tech supply chain to our shores and our state,” said Senator Schumer. “When I wrote and passed into law the CHIPS & Science Act, it was with bringing to the U.S. and New York cutting-edge facilities like this in mind. Four years ago, I personally called on Edwards to locate their new factory along Upstate New York’s emerging semiconductor superhighway. America’s next era of chip manufacturing is underway here in Upstate, and I can confidently say New York’s best days are ahead.” Thanks to an $18 million federal CHIPS grant award from Schumer’s bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law, Edwards Vacuum invested $300+ million in Genesee County and will create 600 good-paying jobs when the facility reaches full production capacity. Schumer explained that all chip fabs need vacuum technology like that produced by Edwards to power the state-of-the-art machine tools and manufacturing equipment needed to make microchips. As a result of this manufacturing investment, new chip fabs such as Micron and GlobalFoundries will have access to critical dry pumps that will now be made in the U.S., offering chip producers shorter wait times, improved responsiveness, lower risks of supply chain disruptions, and reduced CO2 emissions from an American-made product. Schumer has been a relentless champion for expanding the semiconductor supply chain in Western NY. "Edwards’ decision to choose New York means hundreds of good paying jobs and millions of dollars in investment in the Upstate economy while helping to strengthen our domestic semiconductor supply chain and ensuring that New York remains a global hub of innovation and the epicenter of semiconductor manufacturing nationwide." “The opening of our Genesee facility is more than the launch of a new facility. It reflects what is possible when industry, government, and the local community come together with a shared vision,” said Dan Papsidero, General Manager of Edwards Genesee . “We are proud to invest in Genesee County, expand our U.S. manufacturing capabilities, and support the growing semiconductor ecosystem across North America. We thank Senator Schumer and our regional partners for their support in helping make this investment a reality.” Schumer also helped the Buffalo-Rochester-Syracuse region win the prestigious Tech Hub designation to support the buildout of the semiconductor supply chain in Upstate NY through his bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law and last year secured a major $40 million investment to implement the Tech Hub’s work with companies like Edwards. The proposal, called the “NY SMART I-Corridor Tech Hub,” has built on the historic investments Schumer delivered that have spurred a boom in semiconductor manufacturing and innovation across Upstate NY. Edwards Vacuum is working with Genesee Community College and Tech Hub partners like Monroe Community College, Erie Community College, and the Northland Workforce Training Center to help them hire and train hundreds of new workers. Thanks to Schumer’s CHIPS & Science Law, Upstate New York has seen a major revival in tech manufacturing. In the Capital Region, GlobalFoundries is set to receive up to $1.5 billion in direct funding through the bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law to support the expansion of its existing fab in Malta and the construction of a second fab, in addition to up to $375 million in federal funding to launch Quantum Technology Solutions, a new quantum business within GlobalFoundries that will position America at the forefront of technology innovation. GlobalFoundries partner PsiQuantum finalized an award of up to $100 million to expand research and development spearheaded out of the Air Force Research Laboratory in Rome. IBM is set to receive up to $1 billion in federal CHIPS R&D funding to form a new entity to operate a secure 300mm quantum wafer fab at Albany NanoTech. Micron has broken ground for a historic $100+ billion investment to build a cutting-edge memory fab in Central New York with the support of an over $6 billion CHIPS agreement. Corning Incorporated finalized a $32 million agreement to make a $315 million investment that would increase production at its Canton facility of specialized glass vital for the semiconductor industry. TTM Technologies, a printed circuit board manufacturer, plans to invest up to $130 million to expand its facilities in Onondaga County, creating up to 400 good-paying jobs, supported by $30 million in federal investment that Schumer delivered. Schumer secured $1.5 billion for Wolfspeed to boost domestic silicon carbide production in the Mohawk Valley. ###

After Nearly Two Years Of Plummeting Tourism, Skyrocketing Costs, And Small Businesses Paying The Price For Harmful Trade Policies, Schumer Says Central & Northern NY Are On Frontlines Of Trade War And Tariffs Must End Now Schumer’s New Bill – The End Trump’s Tariff Tax Act – Would Terminate Trump’s Latest Round Of Global And 50% Canadian Tariffs To Deliver Lower Costs For Families, Seniors, & Small Businesses Schumer To Trump: Dump These Damaging Tariffs To Lower Costs & Forget Renaming Our Beloved Lake Ontario With Trump’s tariffs driving nearly two straight years of declining tourism and skyrocketing costs, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today stood at the Port of Oswego Authority with a bipartisan coalition of Central and Northern New York business owners, public officials, and concerned community members being crushed by Trump’s tariff war to launch his new legislation – the End Trump’s Tariff Tax Act – to revoke and refund Trump’s most recent tariffs, including 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. Schumer said that as Trump makes threats to annex Canada and rename Upstate New York’s beloved Lake Ontario, costs for families and local businesses are skyrocketing. The Senator said his bill is key to reversing the damage done by Trump’s tariffs, stopping this nonsensical trade war, and lowering costs for Upstate New York’s families and small businesses. “Costs are skyrocketing, small businesses are being squeezed, and family farms are getting hammered because of Trump’s tariff taxes and costly trade war. But, instead of making life more affordable for hardworking families, Trump is focused on directing more taxpayer dollars to his billionaire friends while doubling down on his misguided effort to rename our beloved Lake Ontario and threat to make Canada the 51 st state,” said Senator Schumer. “In Central New York, legacy businesses and employers from the Port of Oswego to Eagle Metalcraft have already lost millions of dollars in revenue, and small businesses from Sterling Family Farm to 114 Reserve are struggling through tens of thousands of dollars in unforeseen expenses that are slowing growth and squeezing margins. That’s why I’m here announcing my bill to immediately end this tariff war and bring down the skyrocketing costs. We can’t let this nonsensical trade war with Canada, our closest trading partner and ally, continue. It’s a gut punch to Central New York businesses, to New York’s economy, and to American families that are being hit hard by Trump’s tariff temper tantrums.” In July, Trump levied 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods, including products that had previously been protected by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) that Trump opted not to renew. Schumer said this follows a series of unnecessary provocations directed toward our closest trading partner, ally, and neighbor to the north, Canada. Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario ‘Lake America’ and has repeatedly threatened to make Canada its 51 st state. As a result of Trump’s escalating tariff war, Canadians are canceling trips to the United States , and tourism has declined across all the major bridge ports of entry between New York and Canada compared to 2024. Schumer declared it is time to put an end to Trump’s trade war with Canada that is hurting communities across America and raising costs for working families. Schumer said Americans are paying the price for Trump’s policies and being crushed by rising costs caused by Trump’s tariff taxes and costly trade war. Data released earlier this month found that families have had to spend an additional $6,000 on everyday essentials under Trump due to rising prices for housing, groceries, gas, electricity, healthcare, and more. Schumer’s End Trump’s Tariff Tax Act would revoke and refund President Trump’s latest barrage of tariffs and repeal the archaic authorities he has used to continue his trade war. This legislation would apply to President Trump’s recent Section 301 tariffs on 60 countries, previously imposed Section 122 temporary global tariffs, and the 50% Canadian tariffs. Businesses across Central and Northern New York are feeling renewed pain as a result of the Trump Administration’s latest barrage of tariffs, including: The Port of Oswego Authority, located on the shores of Lake Ontario directly across from Canada, has been hit especially hard, losing upwards of $1 million in potential revenue as a result of the administration’s tariffs and trade war. The port is worried that if the tariffs and trade war continue, it will make it increasingly difficult to invest in the infrastructure needed to be prepared for an influx of demand on Central NY’s horizon with Micron and other new manufacturing investments underway across the region. Eagle Metalcraft , a multi-generational metal fabricator located in Syracuse, has lost millions of dollars as a result of tariffs. Though the administration claims its tariffs will bring new businesses into the United States, Eagle Metalcraft reports that the opposite is happening to its business. Eagle Metalcraft said that it lost 50% of revenue from one of its primary customers, who moved manufacturing and much of its purchasing to Asia to avoid the impact of tariffs, and was forced to go through two rounds of layoffs and part ways with six employees. Sterling House Farm , a small, multi-generational family farm with land in Cayuga and St. Lawrence Counties, has felt the pain of rising costs and uncertainty caused by tariffs on lumber, equipment, and fertilizer both personally and across their community. In order to complete a new greenhouse in Sterling, the farm had to move its business from local lumber yards like Ace Hardware in Oswego to specialty mills to avoid surging prices caused by tariffs, turning what was expected to be a one-season build into a multi-year endeavor that ran thousands of dollars over budget. 114 Reserve , a small café and community hub located in Fulton, is paying $1 more per pound for coffee beans and nearly 50% more for heavy whipping cream and oat milk, as well as significant markups on syrup, cocoa, electricity, and paper products driven by tariffs and the trade war with Canada. With customers already facing increased costs on everything from their gasoline to their grocery store bill, 114 Reserve has been unable to raise prices, which has led to shrinking margins, thousands of dollars in lost profit, and prevented the hiring of new staff. "On behalf of the Port of Oswego and community we serve, I would like to thank Senator Schumer for his leadership in fighting back against the negative effects that this administration’s tariffs on Canada are having on the port, our customers, local workers, and the Central New York economy,” said Port of Oswego Executive Director Tom Drumm . “The harmful and unnecessary trade war caused by these tariffs directly hampers the port’s ability to carry out its core business, translating into more than $1 million of lost potential revenue, increased volatility in demand and order flow, and fewer hours for our best in class maritime workforce. It has also frustrated the port’s plans for the growth and modernization needed to support Central NY’s ongoing manufacturing renaissance. I am proud to stand with Senator Schumer and the bipartisan coalition he assembled on our docks to push for passage of federal legislation that will end the trade war with Canada, stabilize costs, and protect working families.” “Owning a small business in Central NY is no small thing to us here in Fulton. At 114 Reserve, we are proud to have created a space for people to gather, a chance to experience locally roasted coffee, and a healthy source of jobs in our community. However, our café has been heavily impacted by the significant new taxes and tariffs across our industry, which have caused extreme price increases on dairy, cocoa, coffee beans, electricity, and paper products while we are being squeezed by increased shipping and gasoline costs at the very same time,” said 114 Reserve Owner and Operator Mikaela Tubolino . “These increases are not only felt by our suppliers, roasters, and bakers, but by our customers who are already struggling with affordability in their everyday lives. We have done our best to hold off on raising prices with the hope that relief would come soon, but as time has passed the losses have added up to thousands of dollars, eating into our bottom line and preventing us from hiring new staff. I appreciate Senator Schumer for standing up for small businesses like 114 Reserve and pushing to end the tariffs to bring down the cost of goods we depend on.” According to the Senator, even municipalities like the City of Oswego are feeling the negative impacts of tariffs and the trade war with Canada. After generations of Canadian families traveled to the City of Oswego to vacation, attend events, enjoy the waterfront, and support local businesses, the city says that it has seen a substantial decline in Canadian visitors over the last year. The city reports that local businesses from the Oswego Speedway to local shops, restaurants, hotels, museums, charter fishing operations, and more are feeling the negative effects of fewer visitors, creating an added challenge for business owners and their employees. The city says that impact is also felt directly, as the drop in economic activity has decreased the city’s sales tax revenue, which is a critical source of funding used for essential services and to keep pressure off local property taxpayers. Schumer continues to be one of the leading advocates in Congress to end this unnecessary, damaging trade war with Canada that is decimating Upstate NY’s economy, tourism, small businesses, and local jobs. Last year, Schumer twice used a special fast-track process to force a vote in the Senate to end Trump’s destructive trade war with Canada. More specifically, Schumer has a long history of fighting back against the Trump Administration’s misguided and poorly implemented tariff policies in Central and Northern NY. Last year, Schumer stood at 1812 on the River in Sackett’s Harbor and the Emerald Cocktail Kitchen in Syracuse to push for an end to the administration’s sweeping International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariffs – which were ultimately found to be unconstitutional by the U.S. Supreme Court – alongside small businesses from across the region, including: 1812 Brewing Company in Watertown had its award-winning, American-made craft beer ripped off Ontario shelves in response to tariffs on Canada, slashing 10-15% of the company’s total business overnight, decreasing the company’s 2025 sales by at least $100,000 in 2025, and undoing years of hard work and investment to break into the Canadian market. Talking Cursive Brewing Company, a small craft brewery located in Syracuse, has faced significant challenges from higher prices on the aluminum cans they import from Canada to more expensive hops and grain imported from the EU, Australia, and New Zealand. After the administration’s initial round of tariffs in early 2025, Talking Cursive experienced a sharp decline in customers, sales, and the biggest first-quarter downturn in its seven years of operation. Apothecary Chocolates in Colton was forced to close its doors and lay off three full-time employees after tariffs surged the price of a bag of its specialty chocolate by more than 180% – from $125 in 2024 to over $350 as of August 2025. Monthly Boxer in Watertown has faced a significant downtick in customer volume, order flow, and total revenue, which the company attributes directly to tariff rates and their volatility. The company says customers are downsizing, delaying, and even cancelling orders because of tariff-driven uncertainty in pricing and demand. Lake & River Roasters in Cape Vincent has watched adversarial rhetoric and trade policies aimed at Canada and other key trading partners drive away friends, family and repeat customers from across the border, as tariffs have doubled the average price of their imported coffee beans – from around $3 per pound to $6 or more – in less than one year. This has forced the company to either charge more for impacted products at the risk of pricing out customers or absorb the added costs at the risk of operating on unsustainable margins. With every economic data point flashing red because of Trump’s chaotic trade war, Schumer called on New York’s House Republicans to stand up for Upstate NY businesses and working families footing the bill for Trump’s tariff tax. Under Schumer’s leadership, Senate Democrats are also pushing for tariff exemptions for small businesses and putting an end to Trump’s across-the-board tariffs, and Schumer has co-led amicus briefs in the lawsuit challenging Trump’s authority to levy tariffs. Schumer said ending this costly trade war is key to protecting American families from price increases and job losses. ###

Trump and Congressional Republicans promised lower health care costs, but instead they delivered soaring premiums, sky-high deductibles, and coverage ripped away from millions,” said Senator Schumer. “Now, they’ve kicked more than 46,000 New Yorkers in the Hudson Valley off their insurance plan, and many cannot afford alternatives. Schumer added, “I’m proud to be working with the entire New York Democratic delegation in the fight against Trump’s callous and calculated policies that have ripped health insurance away from families and made life harder for hardworking New Yorkers. Trump and spineless rubber-stamp Republicans in Congress cut $1 trillion from your health care and food assistance to fund a tax cut for billionaires – and they specifically targeted New York’s Essential Plan, ripping healthcare from more than 15,000 people in our district,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “It’s cruel, un-American, and the exact opposite of everything our community stands for. On behalf of the 450,000 New Yorkers kicked off their insurance, we’re fighting back. I’m incredibly proud to join our entire state Democratic delegation in introducing this legislation to reverse the cuts, restore your coverage, and send a clear message to Trump: Don’t mess with New York.” “When people lose access to their healthcare, we all lose. It often shows up in people delaying care until preventable conditions become dire emergencies, flooding ERs and driving up healthcare costs for everyone. Nearly half a million New Yorkers have lost their health insurance because of Congressional Republicans’ H.R. 1. That is unconscionable and the antithesis of government’s most fundamental responsibility to protect the people it serves. I thank Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and the entire New York Democratic Delegation for fighting to reverse this damage through the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act. Congress must pass this legislation and restore health insurance for New Yorkers who never should have lost it in the first place,” said NYS Senator Michelle Hinchey. “Families who got kicked off the Essential Plan but need coverage are paying $800 per month in premiums for plans that barely do anything, and some have even chosen to take a pay cut so that they can qualify for Medicaid. Major Fed $$ Will Help Eliminate Potential For Accidents At Crossing, That Sees More Than 7,400 Vehicles And 100+ Train Crossings Per Day, By Building New Overpass Following Horrific 2015 Valhalla Crash That Killed Six People, Schumer Vowed To Boost Rail Crossing Safety In The Hudson Valley; Schumer Says Funds – From “Rail Crossing Elimination Grant Program” Created By The Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law He Championed – Will Put Safety On The Right Track For Countless Drivers And Metro-North Passengers Annually Schumer: New Castle And Chappaqua Are On Track For Major Rail Crossing Safety Improvements! U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today announced a whopping $107,712,000 in federal funding to support the grade separation of Roaring Brook Road along the Metro-North Railroad’s Harlem Line in New Castle, adjacent to Chappaqua, eliminating the potential for accidents at a notoriously dangerous crossing. The funding comes from the Rail Crossing Elimination Grant Program created by Schumer’s Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law. “A whopping $107 million in federal funding is on track to make major safety improvements in Westchester County in New Castle and Chappaqua! Schumer And Morelle Have Long Supported Department Of Defense’s Manufacturing Engineering Education Program (MEEP), Which Has Now Delivered $10+ Million For Monroe Community College Schumer Fought To Secure Boosts In FY26 Federal Budget For Critical DoD Program To Strengthen MCC’s World-Class Optics & Photonics Engineering Programs, Giving Workers The Skills They Need For Good-Paying, Hi-Tech Local Jobs Schumer, Morelle: New Fed $$ Is A Win-Win For Rochester-Finger Lakes Workforce, Local Businesses & America’s National Security U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer and U.S. Congressman Joe Morelle today announced a $5,383,256 three-year grant award for Monroe Community College’s (MCC) optics program from the U.S. Department of Defense’s (DoD) Manufacturing Engineering Education Program (MEEP).
