The Rochester-Finger Lakes region has a proud history of excellence and innovation in optics and photonics. This federal award will support Monroe Community College’s associate degree program in optics engineering, one of the first and only of its kind in the country,” said Senator Schumer. “Three years ago, I was proud to secure a critical increase in the federal budget to keep MCC’s optics training program running to train the next generation of optics technicians needed to support the high-tech manufacturing and semiconductor businesses that we are bringing to Upstate New York. Today, we are building on that success by connecting local students to good-paying jobs in Rochester.” “A strong workforce is the foundation of a strong economy, and Monroe Community College is helping prepare the next generation of skilled workers for success,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “This $5.3 million investment will open doors to good-paying careers, strengthen our local Optics, Photonics, Imaging, and Lasers ecosystem, and bolster our national security. I’m proud to have secured this critical funding and continue building a stronger future for Rochester.” “Monroe Community College is deeply grateful to Senator Schumer and Congressman Morelle for their continued advocacy and investment in our students, our institution, and the economic future of our region. This $5.3 million investment will help MCC expand access to high-quality education, hands-on training, and apprenticeship opportunities in the rapidly growing optics and photonics industries. Our optics program is a cornerstone of the Sydor Optics Advanced Technology Center, which was also made possible through previous federal funding championed by our federal delegation. We are especially grateful for their sustained commitment to building MCC's capacity to educate and train the next generation of skilled professionals. As a national leader in precision optics education, MCC is uniquely positioned to connect talented students with meaningful, family-sustaining careers while helping employers meet critical workforce needs. This latest investment builds upon that strong foundation and further reinforces Rochester's position as a national center for optics innovation and advanced manufacturing,” said Dr. DeAnna R. Burt-Nanna, President of Monroe Community College. Schumer and Morelle explained that the DoD’s MEEP invests in programs that better position the current and next-generation manufacturing workforce vital for our nation’s defense innovation ecosystem and components that assure defense technological superiority. This is the third time MCC has been awarded funding through the MEEP program, as the nation’s first community college to administer associate degrees in precision optics. With this latest round of funding, MCC will be able to strengthen its existing program to grow the national workforce for the optics industry and give workers the skills they need for careers with major local employers in the region in the optics, photonics, and semiconductor industries. Specifically, MCC seeks to grow enrollment for this program for the in-demand optics industry and establish new training and apprenticeship opportunities. Schumer and Morelle have been longtime advocates for Monroe Community College’s optics and photonics degree programs. In 2017, following their relentless advocacy , the lawmakers secured over $550,000 from the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Advanced Technology Foundation’s Education program for MCC to expand its optics and photonics degree programs, purchase new equipment, as well as develop a new curriculum and expand student outreach. In 2023, the lawmakers secured more than $5 million over three years for the program, made possible by their work securing $15 million in federal funding in FY23 for the DoD’s Manufacturing Engineering Education Program (MEEP), allowing MCC to apply for the funding they received in 2023. Similarly, this year, the lawmakers secured a $15 million boost in the MEEP program in the federal Fiscal Year 2026 Defense Appropriations Bill, and then personally advocated with DoD to push for MCC to compete and ultimately secure this new $5.3 million funding award to grow its training program. This over $10M in MEEP funding has been instrumental in enabling MCC to supercharge its optics training program to significantly expand its program, create new skilled jobs, and provide local optics manufacturers with the vital workers they need. Specifically, thanks to this MEEP funding, the MCC optics program has been able to increase its student enrollment by 3,520 percent since 2015. This first-of-its-kind in the nation two-year training program provides a direct path to employment for hundreds of students and supports the lawmakers’ success in growing the semiconductor industry across Upstate New York. A copy of the lawmakers’ letter in support of this MCC grant award to Dr. Jagadeesh Pamulapati, Principal Director for Science and Technology (S&T) Foundations, Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering is below: We are pleased to write in support of Monroe Community College’s (MCC) pursuit to successfully apply and secure an award from the Department of Defense’s Manufacturing Engineering Education Program (MEEP) for MCC’s proposal, FOCUS-D: Fortifying Optics Capabilities for U.S. Security & Defense. Such funding will enable MCC to build on the success of MCC’s previous 2023 MEEP award, DEEPER OPS, to strengthen and expand educational training to prepare even more technicians for defense-relevant manufacturing and the domestic defense supply chain while helping to reverse the current nationwide shortage of these skilled optics workers who are in high demand with defense-relevant employers to support the nation’s domestic supply chain. Monroe Community College is uniquely positioned to carry out this important work. Located in Rochester, New York, MCC is the nation’s first college to award associate degrees in precision optics and has built a strong foundation for technician education, workforce development, and employer-connected training. The Finger Lakes region is a nationally significant hub for optics, photonics, imaging, advanced manufacturing, and semiconductor activity, with more than 150 related companies and continued demand for skilled optics workers. We were pleased to help secure additional FY26 MEEP funding in order to provide continued support for the vital work done by MEEP grantees, including Monroe Community College to train workers to fill the jobs needed across the defense industrial domestic supply chain. By leveraging MCC’s nationally recognized optics workforce training programs, MCC’s FOCUS-D proposal will not only build on its proven successes of turning out well-prepared technicians to enter the defense supply chain workforce, but will accelerate and increase these training and career placement results with a stronger alignment to military, defense, and space applications, and deeper employer-connected pathways. MCC has already demonstrated strong results through its Optical Systems Technology program and prior federal support, including increased enrollment, expanded credential attainment, dual-enrollment pathways for high school students, and direct engagement with employers across the defense supply chain. MCC has long been one of Rochester’s great engines of opportunity, translating local talent into nationally significant skill. With funding, MCC will enhance and expand its optics technician curriculum, accelerate flexible pathways into the field, modernize defense-relevant laboratory instruction, and deepen partnerships with defense employers through paid internships, apprenticeships, and employer-connected training. The project will support apprentices, incumbent workers, veterans, adult learners, career changers, and students entering the workforce, while expanding training in areas critical to military, defense, and space applications, including optical coatings, metrology, contamination control, infrared materials, high-energy optics, and directed energy systems. By growing a stronger pipeline of skilled technicians, MCC’s proposal will create a win-win for students and businesses in the optics supply chain: workers gain access to high-quality careers, while employers gain the trained talent needed to meet defense manufacturing need. ###

Senators Say NYS&W Main Line Is A Key Corridor For Freight Rail Needed To Support Central NY Businesses And Major Manufacturing Projects Like Micron Thanks To Schumer’s Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, New Fed Investment Will Help NYS&W Upgrade Infrastructure Between Cortland And Virgil Schumer, Gillibrand: Getting CNY Rail Infrastructure Back On Track! After Schumer two years ago stood in Cortland to tout major federal funding to upgrade rail infrastructure in Cortland and Onondaga Counties, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand today announced that the New York, Susquehanna & Western Railway (NYS&W) has received an additional $3,168,302 in federal funding to make critical improvements to the Main Line between Cortland and Virgil. The federal funding today comes from the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. This award brings the total federal investment in NYSW’s project to $13,528,522, including $3,961,750 in FY23-24 CRISI funding , $3,467,348 in FY22 CRISI funding , and $2,931,122 in FY21 CRISI funding, all a direct result of the historic increases in funding for the program Schumer fought to secure in the Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law. The NYS&W operates over 400 miles of track in New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania and is 286,000-pound gross weight capable on all lines. NYS&W serves over 85 customers and transports a wide range of commodities such as feed ingredients, lumber, and other building materials, chemicals, and aggregates for customers in New York State. ###

New Fed Funding Includes $11M To Replace Ten Miles Of Track In Wayne County And Nearly $10M To Replace Forty Miles Of Track Between Brockport And Lockport Funding Comes From U.S. Department Of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure And Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program, Which Senators Boosted In Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law Schumer, Gillibrand: Getting Rochester-Finger Lakes Rail On Track For Safer Future! U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand announced $20,843,235 in federal funding to make critical improvements to rail infrastructure in the Rochester-Finger Lakes region. The funding includes $11.2 million for the Ontario Midland Railroad and $9.6 million for the Falls Road Railroad. This federal investment comes from the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program that the Senators fought to boost funding for in the Bipartisan Infrastructure and Jobs Law. “This more than $20 million puts the Rochester-Finger Lakes region on track for a safer future. Thanks to significant federal funding from my Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, New York railroad companies from Lockport to Wayne County now have the resources they need to repair aging tracks that the region’s top employers, including Coca-Cola Fairlife, Xerox, Keurig Dr. Pepper/Motts, and more, rely on to grow,” said Senator Schumer. “These rail upgrades mean fewer trucks on the road, lower fuel consumption, and more jobs. I will continue fighting to deliver federal support for the infrastructure improvements Upstate New York needs.” “This critical $20-plus million investment thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law will upgrade tens of miles of track across the Rochester–Finger Lakes region, ensuring our rail system is safer, faster, and more reliable,” said Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies (THUD) . “From Wayne County to Brockport and Lockport, our local railways keep New Yorkers and our businesses moving. These critical repairs will strengthen our supply chains, protect good-paying jobs, and help drive economic growth across Upstate New York.” Ontario Midland Railroad (OMID) received $11,200,000 for the Wayne County Mainline Safety and Reliability Project, which will modernize deteriorating rail infrastructure while advancing several crucial long-term goals for OMID. The project will rehabilitate an approximately 10-mile segment of track in Wayne County, replace approximately nine miles of rail, resurface eight at-grade crossings, replace seven turnouts, remove three turnouts, and perform associated ballast placement, tamping, and surfacing. These improvements will reduce truck traffic, lower fuel consumption, and support workforce growth and economic development. Schumer urged U.S. Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) Administrator David Fink to deliver this funding for the Rochester-Finger Lakes region. Ontario Midland Railroad provides important freight rail service to agricultural, manufacturing, transload, and other commercial customers across the region. Schumer explained that current aging infrastructure creates an operational bottleneck, hindering efficiency and long-term success of the businesses and industries that rely on this corridor. Upgrading the East-West line will be the key to unlocking new job growth and sales opportunities for many of the region’s top employers, including the Coca-Cola Fairlife milk factory and Xerox’s campus in the town of Webster in Monroe County, as well as many of Wayne County’s top employers, including Keurig Dr. Pepper/Motts production facility, Sodus Cold Storage facility, and Fleishmann’s Vinegar factory. This upgrade would, in turn, benefit the economy of the overall area served by Ontario Midland Railroad and is key to the success of many of the region’s top employers, including Thatcher Chemical, Baldwin Richardson Foods, CRC Polymer Systems, Maco Packaging, K.M. Davies Co., and Nutrien Ag, which is a major supplier of fertilizer to local Wayne County farms, and more. This project would provide a critical boost in our efforts to grow new jobs and ensure on-time delivery of raw materials and on-time shipment of these companies’ products to market. Upgrades will enhance rail safety and streamline network performance, crucial to maintaining supply-chain continuity in a demanding modern economy. "We are profoundly grateful to Senators Schumer and Gillibrand for their relentless advocacy and partnership in securing this critical 2025–2026 grant for the Ontario Midland Railroad. This federal support is a game-changer for our operations, ensuring we can maintain safe, reliable service and continue driving economic growth across the communities we proudly serve. They understand how vital robust short-line rail infrastructure is to Upstate New York, and we thank our Senators for standing with OMID to secure our future,” said Robert Babcock, Chairman, and Jeffrey Bauman, President of the Ontario Midland Railroad (OMID). “We are pleased that the Federal Railroad Administration has approved the Ontario Midland Railroad’s application for funding under the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements Program. This funding will support comprehensive modernization of Ontario Midland Railroad’s east-west corridor by replacing aging infrastructure with new rail and crossties. These upgrades are essential to eliminating current operational bottlenecks and improving track integrity, which in turn drives greater transportation efficiency across the Greater Rochester, NY region. By revitalizing this line, the project ensures our local manufacturing, agricultural, and transload partners have access to the high-capacity, resilient rail service they need to compete in today’s economy,” said Matt Hurlbutt, President and CEO of Greater Rochester Enterprise. Brian Pincelli, Executive Director, Wayne County Economic Development & Planning, said, “Rail infrastructure is a significant element of economic development, and the OMID system supports key Wayne County agricultural and manufacturing industries. This funding will allow OMID to make key modernization investments that will serve the current and future county economy by removing existing operational bottlenecks, enhancing track integrity, and improving transportation efficiency throughout the region.” In addition, Falls Road Railroad Co. received $9,643,235 for the Falls Branch Track, Crossing, & Bridge Project. The project includes the rehabilitation of approximately 40 miles of track and rail infrastructure between Brockport and Lockport. The project will replace rail and ties, add ballast, resurface main line track, rehabilitate a bridge, and resurface six at-grade crossings. The Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, which Schumer crafted and led to passage in the Senate, included $5 billion over five years for the CRISI program. The program invests in various projects within the United States to improve railroad safety, efficiency, and reliability; mitigate congestion at both intercity passenger and freight rail chokepoints to support more efficient travel and goods movement; enhance multi-modal connections; and lead to new or substantially improved Intercity Passenger Rail Transportation corridors. ###

Federal Funding Will Help Van Cortlandt Manor Support HVAC Upgrades And Help Creek Meeting House Install Efficient Heat Pump Heating System Both Historical Sites Tell Stories About The Hudson Valley’s Role In The American Revolution Schumer: Fed $$ Will Ensure Hudson Valley History Can Be Preserved For Generations To Come U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today delivered $1,281,961 in federal funding for critical repairs to Van Cortlandt Manor in Croton-On-Hudson and the Creek Meeting House in Dutchess County through the National Park Service’s Semiquincentennial Grant Program. Schumer explained that federal funding for Van Cortlandt Manor is especially important as it hosts its annual Great Jack O'Lantern Blaze, featuring thousands of hand-carved pumpkins and welcoming more than 100,000 visitors each Halloween season. Schumer said that as the country celebrates America’s 250 th birthday this year, this federal funding will help preserve two beloved Hudson Valley historical sites for generations to come. “Van Cortlandt Manor and the Creek Meeting House both tell the story of life in the Hudson Valley during the American Revolution. Every year, these sites bring hundreds of thousands of visitors to the Hudson Valley,” said Senator Schumer. “I’m proud to deliver this $1.2 million in federal funding in honor of our nation’s 250 th anniversary so that these national treasures have the resources they need to continue attracting visitors to Upstate New York and teaching them about the history of the United States.” “We are grateful to Senator Schumer for his strong support this NPS semi quincentennial grant for the restoration of the Creek Meeting House built in 1777. Now we can look forward to another 250 years of this historic building serving our community as a gathering place and educational center,” said Cynthia Koch, President, Town of Clinton Historical Society. “Van Cortlandt Manor holds a special place in early American history as the home of prominent Patriot politicians during the Revolutionary War and as an embodiment of the cultures, ideas, and debates that shaped the nascent nation. We are so grateful to the National Park Service for this grant, which will allow us to undertake crucial preservation work to ensure that the site will educate and engage visitors for many generations to come,” said Waddell Stillman, President of Historic Hudson Valley. Schumer explained how this funding will be used to support critical upgrades to Van Cortlandt Manor and Creek Meeting House: Van Cortlandt Manor , a National Historic Landmark, was originally inhabited by the Van Cortlandt family, who were one of New York’s most prominent families that included powerful colonial landlords, Patriot army officers in the American Revolution, and politicians who helped shape the new nation. Their lives and the site’s history are well-documented and shared with the public through fact-based, hands-on educational programming. This $694,500 in federal funding will support HVAC upgrades, replace the failing heating system, and allow Historic Hudson Valley to continue its longstanding partnerships with the Village of Croton-on-Hudson and local historians. Schumer’s letter of support can be found here. The Creek Meeting House was built out of fieldstone by members of the Society of Friends (Quakers) in 1777–1780, during the height of the Revolutionary War in New York. The Creek Meeting House is part of the little-known history of the roots of the anti-slavery movement in Revolutionary-era New York. The house is a crucial monument recognizing the long and difficult fight for civil rights in the United States. This $587,461 in federal funding will replace an outworn oil furnace with an efficient heat pump heating system and install insulation and storm windows for the first time. Schumer’s letter of support can be found here. The National Park Service’s Semiquincentennial Grant Program seeks to honor America’s 250th Anniversary by restoring sites on the National Register of Historic Places that commemorate the nation’s founding. ###

Schumer Seeks Assurances From Verizon That New Yorkers—Including Seniors, Residents On Fixed Incomes, and Small Businesses—Won’t Face Higher Costs And Be Forced To Pay More For Essential Phone Service Schumer Says Alternative Equipment Must Provide Reliable Emergency Service & 911 Access During Power Outages, Especially For Residents In Rural Communities With Limited Connectivity Schumer To Verizon: Landlines Are Lifelines As Verizon transitions away from copper-wire landlines , generating widespread confusion and concern for many New Yorkers, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today called on Verizon to ensure that all New Yorkers have uninterrupted, reliable service, are protected from higher costs, and will be provided transparency from the company about what any new, alternative technologies might mean for them, including their ability to contact emergency services and stay connected during power outages. Verizon is currently seeking approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to discontinue legacy plain old telephone service (POTS) delivered over copper. Customers in New York who utilize copper-wire landlines, many of whom are seniors as well as residents of rural communities, are worried about what this means for the reliability and accessibility of service. Schumer demanded answers from Verizon and said the company must engage with residents to ensure there are no safety, reliability, and connectivity challenges. “As Verizon moves to transition away from copper landlines, Upstate New Yorkers are concerned about losing a vital connection. They deserve clear answers about what this means for their ability to stay connected and make ends meet. That’s why I’m turning up the volume on Verizon, demanding transparency, affordability, and a commitment to working with communities to make sure this critical service is not interrupted for customers now connected via copper landlines,” said Senator Schumer. “Verizon must guarantee that this transition will not mean higher costs—especially for seniors, residents on fixed incomes, or small businesses—and that any alternative options will provide reliable service to contact emergency services, including during power outages. This is crucial in rural Upstate communities where there are limited connectivity options.” Verizon is currently transitioning away from copper-wire landlines, which can be expensive and time-consuming to repair, according to the company, towards other alternatives like fiber, fixed wireless, cellular wireless, and satellite. Currently, the company is sending notices to customers in New York and across the country who still use copper landlines. As New Yorkers receive these letters, many residents are worried they will lose service, not have a reliable connection during a time of need, or be forced to pay more if the FCC approves this change. Schumer underscored that for seniors, landlines are lifelines, and that modernizing Verizon’s network should not come at the cost of small businesses and those on fixed incomes. In addition, across Upstate New York, residents in rural communities continue to rely on traditional copper landlines as a critical lifeline during natural disasters and other emergencies. Traditional POTS can remain operational during power outages because the line is powered from the telephone network, rather than solely from electricity in a home. Traditional copper service provides a well-established fixed connection to a specific service address, while replacement technologies can introduce additional questions about wireless coverage, power backup, indoor signal strength, network congestion, and the performance of connected devices during emergencies. For many rural households, cell service is unreliable, and newer, modern infrastructure alternatives like fiber may not yet reach their homes or communities. These reliable landlines are vital for seniors and rural residents to ensure they can contact emergency services when they need them most, especially in areas with weak or nonexistent cellular coverage or access to broadband. Schumer also described how, according to local fire inspectors, there are many small businesses and restaurants that still use copper landlines for their fire alarm dialups. This change could cost these small businesses thousands of dollars to transition to new alternatives, such as cell or internet dialups, depending on the size of the system they need. Some small businesses have or are actively transitioning, but those that have not could potentially face compliance violations and increased costs associated with the change. Schumer explained that Verizon has filed two separate applications seeking authority to discontinue legacy copper-based POTS service. The first covers portions of nine states. A second application filed on September 9 covers portions of nine additional states, including New York, as well as the District of Columbia. Schumer is also urging the FCC to extend the review timeline of the second application, which applies to New York, to ensure that the proposal can be fully assessed and that customers can be directly informed by Verizon as to what any potential changes at their home or business might mean for them. The Communications Workers of America (CWA) has opposed the FCC’s Network Modernization Order under Chairman Brendan Carr, in which the Commission removed essential protections under Section 214, eliminated traditional network change filings, greenlit replacement alternatives such as basic 5/1 Mbps mobile wireless or third-party voice, and preempted state and local regulations that impede service discontinuance. CWA, consumer advocates, and local officials are concerned that dismantling oversight without enforceable protections applicable to major carriers threatens service reliability, 911 emergency access, backup power during outages, and telecommunications jobs. Schumer’s letter to Verizon can be found HERE or below: Dear Mr. Schulman, I write today amid reports that Verizon is seeking approval from the Federal Communications Commission to phase out traditional copper-based landline service. Many residents across New York have already begun receiving notices about the transition from copper to other alternatives and are concerned about what these changes will mean for them. Across Upstate New York, many areas and rural communities have weak or nonexistent cellular coverage or access to broadband. Copper landlines have been essential for rural and senior citizens to stay connected and access help, keep small businesses up and running, and help New Yorkers stay connected in cellular dead zones as well as during power outages. As Verizon begins to transition away from copper landlines for modern alternatives like fiber or wireless, I implore you to ensure no household sees their service interrupted or costs in creased. Furthermore, I request a written response to the following questions that have been raised by constituents and community leaders: Will Verizon physically test service at the customer's premises—or is it relying solely on FCC coverage maps, carrier coverage maps, or database information? What does Verizon consider to be an “equivalent replacement” for a plain old telephone service copper landline? How will the viability of new technologies—such as fiber, wireless, and satellite—be assessed for each address in New York? What is the specific process that Verizon follows when determining if an equivalent replacement is an adequate alternative? Will the replacement remain available during severe weather, extended power outages, cellular network congestion, many calling 911 simultaneously? Will Verizon certify that each proposed replacement technology is compatible with fire alarm communicators, medical alert systems, elevator emergency phones, security systems, fax machines, and other equipment currently connected to copper POTS? How and when will customers be informed of Verizon’s determination regarding whether their residence is equipped to receive an equivalent replacement service? How can customers challenge Verizon’s determination that an equivalent replacement is an adequate alternative? Will Verizon commit to not disconnecting copper connections while a customer is actively disputing the adequacy of the replacement? If replacement equipment fails, and telephone service becomes unable, what is Verizon’s restoration time? How long will Verizon’s replacement service—including battery backup—remain operational during a power outage? What will the total cost to the customer be when the copper landline service is replaced—including all charges, equipment, taxes, installation, activation, battery back-ups, wiring, early termination, bunded-service requirements, and fees? Will Verizon guarantee that customers will not pay more for the replacement service than they currently pay for their plain old telephone landline? Will the price be guaranteed for a specific period of time, or can Verizon increase the rate after the customer is forced to transition? Will customers have an opportunity to demonstrate that the replacement is inadequate based on actual service conditions at their address? Will Verizon commit to conducting additional outreach to rural communities, seniors, customers with disabilities, and small businesses that may have greater difficulty transitioning from copper-based service? While I am encouraged to see Verizon promise continued service to those without FCC-approved alternative equipment, I urge you to transparently engage with customers and work diligently to ensure that customers have all the information they need regarding this proposal. I appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response. ###

This conditional financing commitment further reinforces the importance of Wolfspeed’s operations in Marcy and the long-term opportunities that lie ahead for our region,” said Marc Barraco, Chief of Staff, Mohawk Valley EDGE . The senator fought for and successfully delivered a designation and $40 million implementation award to launch the NY Smart I-Corridor Tech Hub, establishing Upstate NY as a national hub for workforce training, innovation, and manufacturing of semiconductor technologies. A copy of the Schumer-led delegation letter to the Secretary of Defense and Secretary of Commerce is included below: Dear Secretaries Hegseth and Lutnick: We write to draw your attention to a critical matter at the intersection of national security, economic competitiveness and trade policy: the accelerating Chinese government effort to dominate the global silicon carbide semiconductor industry and supply chain, and the urgent need for a whole-of-government response to preserve and strengthen trusted domestic and allied manufacturing of silicon carbide. Silicon carbide is the foundational substrate for a critical class of next-generation semiconductors that are indispensable across advanced defense systems, AI data centers, electric grid infrastructure, 5G telecommunications, and the modern automotive sector. Silicon carbide's unique combination of high-voltage tolerance, thermal conductivity, and switching speed makes it irreplaceable in high-performance air, land and sea propulsion systems, directed energy weapons, and air and missile defense systems. Since launching its Made in China 2025 initiative, Beijing has recognized the military and economic importance of silicon carbide and made global domination in the sector a national industrial priority. In the last five years, Chinese producers have increased their share of the global silicon carbide wafer market from less than 5 percent to nearly 50 percent today. Clearly, China intends to undermine another strategically important industry built on American technology and ingenuity. If this campaign succeeds, the United States will find itself dependent on adversary supply chains for materials essential to our most advanced defense systems and critical technological infrastructure. The domestic supply chain is already under significant pressure and we are at risk of losing industry leaders and globally competitive manufacturers to this coordinated campaign. The time to act is now, before we reach the crisis stage where remedies are impossible or far more expensive and time-consuming. We encourage you to leverage Defense Production Act authorities, critical minerals designations, Buy America requirements, and any other authorities at your disposal to ensure the U.S. can protect its silicon carbide supply chain. ###

Federal Lead Hazard Reduction Program Will Boost Rensselaer County To Help Rid Homes And Communities Of Lead Hazards Schumer Has Long Fought To Get The Lead Out Of Capital Region – Securing Millions In Fed $$ To Remove Lead Hazards From Homes – And Latest Investment Will Boost Efforts Even Further To Rid Homes Across Upstate NY Of Toxic Lead Paint Schumer, Gillibrand: Fed $$$ Is A Shot In The Arm To Protect Western NY’s Children And Public Health U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand today announced $4,410,012.82 from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) Lead Hazard Reduction Program. The senators explained that the funding will be used to address lead-based paint hazards, improving the health of children and families in Rensselaer County. “No amount of toxic lead exposure is safe for children. Today, I am proud to deliver more than $4 million for communities in Rensselaer County to remove lead paint from homes to protect our children and public health,” said Senator Schumer. “Lead poisoning is an irreversible, preventable tragedy that robs many families and children of their future. This major federal funding is the shot in the arm that these regions need to boost lead paint removal and prevention and protect the health and safety of families in Upstate NY.” Everyone deserves a home free of potential health risks, yet thousands of New York families are exposed to dangerous lead paint daily," said Senator Gillibrand, ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Housing Subcommittee. "This exposure is especially harmful to children, who are at disproportionate risk for adverse effects. I'm proud to deliver this funding from the Housing Appropriations bill that I negotiated to help clear hazardous lead paint from homes in Rensselaer County, and I won't stop fighting until lead paint is a relic of the past and no longer a threat to New Yorkers." This funding builds on years of efforts by Schumer to help address toxic lead exposure across the Capital Region. Schumer in 2024 helped secure $5 million for Albany and nearly $4 million for the City of Schenectady through HUD’s Lead Hazard Reduction Program to bolster ongoing efforts. Schumer has long been a driving force in securing federal funding to reduce lead exposure in New York. In addition to fighting lead exposure in paint, Schumer has also led the charge to increase federal funding to eliminate lead service pipes for drinking water in New York. The senator secured one of the largest federal investments ever into eliminating lead service pipes in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Investment & Jobs Law, which includes a $15 billion carve-out within the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (DWSRF) over 5 years ($3 billion every year) for lead service pipe replacement. According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), lead is much more harmful to children than adults because it can affect children’s developing nerves and brains. Lead-based paint, still encasing the walls of many homes, often erodes and settles on children’s toys on the floor, eventually falling into the hands and mouths of children. For children under the age of 6, lead exposure can result in developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioral issues, which may lead to lifelong health and financial consequences. Schumer has long advocated for protecting New York’s children and families in the past by securing millions of dollars in federal funding to eradicate these toxic elements from homes in order to reduce lead poisoning cases. Lead poisoning can cause developmental difficulties, physical pain, and neurological damage. Leader Schumer and Senator Gillibrand, as ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Housing Subcommittee, secured $295.6 million for HUD’s Lead Hazard Reduction Program when negotiating the fiscal year 2026 funding bill that was enacted earlier this year. The purpose of HUD’s Lead Hazard Reduction Program is to identify and control lead-based paint hazards in eligible privately-owned housing for rental or owner-occupants. These grants are used to assist municipalities in carrying out lead hazard control activities. ###

New York Providers Warn That Federal Changes Could Weaken Head Start Programs And Put Essential Services For Families At Risk Schumer Leads Senate Democrats Against Changes That Could Lower Head Start Quality Standards And Hurt New York Families Schumer: Head Start Is Under Attack. We Must Protect It. After a new federal proposal was released earlier this summer that threatens Head Start programs in New York and across the country, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today rallied against the proposed rule with the support of providers from across Upstate New York. Schumer explained the proposed rule would dismantle Head Start by gutting quality standards that ensure that America’s most vulnerable children and families have access to educational programs, medical and dental exams, developmental screenings, and nutrition services. In New York, it is estimated that the proposed rule could lead to 2,854 jobs lost, result in a $12.68 million decline in funding for health services for children and families, and force families to pay $862 more per child for additional childcare. “Roughly 40,000 children in New York benefit from access to Head Start and the early childhood education and comprehensive services it provides families. The proposed changes by the administration threaten the quality of these programs and put essential services at risk. From eliminating math and literacy requirements, to rolling back health services and developmental screenings, and reducing the allowable cap on administrative costs, the gutting of Head Start will hurt hundreds of thousands of children across the country. From DOGE to healthcare, the tendency to cut and gut, rather than to boost and build is sadly reflective of this administration’s misguided approach to governing in general,” said Senator Schumer. “That is why I’m leading Senate Democrats in the fight to stand up against this effort that undercuts Head Start and undercuts our children and makes hardworking families pay the price. We must protect Head Start and invest in New York families.” Earlier this summer, the Trump administration released a new proposal that would gut federal performance standards for Head Start. The proposed rule would eliminate federal requirements that ensure low-income families have access to school readiness resources for children from birth to age five, including, but not limited to: Eliminating staff-to-child ratios. The proposed rule eliminates federal group size and staff-to-child ratios, meaning that Head Start staff may be expected to care for up to 32% more children. Significantly reducing program hours. The proposed rule reduces the number of hours that Head Start programs are required to operate, meaning that families will be forced to find care elsewhere and spend $862 more annually per child on care. Removing requirements to provide comprehensive health care services and developmental screenings. The proposed rule removes requirements around connecting children and families with health, mental health, dental, visions, screenings, and other related support services, forcing families to find these services elsewhere and pay higher prices. Lowering the allowable cap on administrative costs from 15% to 5%. The proposed rule lowers the allowable cap that programs can spend on administrative costs from 15% to 5%, meaning that programs will be forced to bring their administrative costs (staff salary and benefits, auditing, accounting, human resources, etc.) down to 5% of their grant amount. Many programs will be forced to institute layoffs and pay cuts, and some programs may no longer find it finally viable to operate, especially small and rural programs. Head Start experts say the proposed changes would weaken the quality of Head Starts services and undermine early childhood education. Currently, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), which runs Head Start programs, is holding a 60-day comment period for its proposed rule. An initial analysis based on HHS data estimate that nationally, the proposed rule means that nearly 40,000 Head Start jobs could be cut, Head Start staff could experience a 6-9% pay cut even while being expected to care for up to 32% more children, and healthcare services for children and families could be reduced by up to $167 million annually. The senator announced he will continue to lead Senate Democrats in the fight to stand up against the proposed changes to Head Start, programs that serve approximately 40,000 children in New York and over 685,000 children nationally every year. The senator said maintaining high-quality standards for Head Start programs is essential for the success of kids in New York and across the country. Schumer’s leadership has garnered the support of providers serving children across Upstate New York. In the Capital Region , there are concerns that the federal requirements could create inconsistent quality and protections across Head Start programs, resulting in different implementation standards. The Fulmont Head Start Program, which is funded to serve 182 three- and four-year-old children every year, served 213 children and families last year. "Head Start standards are not just paperwork or regulations—they are the promise that every child, no matter their ZIP code, deserves a strong start in life. We can reduce unnecessary bureaucracy without lowering the floor of quality that families depend on. That’s why this NPRM matters: the choices we make today will shape the quality, consistency, and access of Head Start for children and families for years to come. Thank you, Senator Schumer, for taking the time to focus on this important issue and for standing up for the children, families, and communities who rely on Head Start. Your leadership and willingness to engage on this issue truly matter. We appreciate your commitment to making sure that every child has the opportunity for a strong start," said Denis Wilson, Sr., Executive Director/CEO of Fulmont Community Action Agency. In Western New York, federal funding reductions have already resulted in cuts, including the loss of jobs and available Head Start slots. “Community Action Organization of WNY’s Head Start and Early Head Start programs are far more than childcare; they are a comprehensive system of education, health, mental health, nutrition, disability, workforce, and family-stability services. CAO serves more than 1,000 children and families in Erie and Niagara counties. The proposed federal cuts and the removal of key Head Start requirements would significantly weaken our program quality, reduce safety and eliminate the individualized comprehensive support services, which are all the hallmark of Head Start. Head Start programs are a proven community investment that strengthens children, families, and the local workforce while promoting long-term stability. Almost 200 slots for children with disabilities would be eliminated. If enacted, cuts will absolutely force us to lay off staff, close classrooms and sites, thereby decreasing access to early childhood education in communities already facing childcare shortages. These proposed cuts are simply unconscionable: they are harmful to children, families, and communities. CAO of WNY is grateful for the continued leadership of Senator Schumer in advocating on the behalf of Head Start and the children, families and communities they serve,” said Dr. Marie Cannon, President and CEO of Community Action Organization of Western New York. "Head Start is far more than a preschool program. It provides children and families with comprehensive services that support school readiness, health, nutrition, developmental screenings, and family stability. At Community Action of Orleans & Genesee, we see every day how these services change lives and strengthen communities. While there is significant discussion about increasing Head Start enrollment, policymakers must recognize the realities facing families in states like New York. A parent working full-time at New York's minimum wage can earn above the federal poverty guidelines used to determine Head Start eligibility, even while struggling to afford housing, childcare, transportation, and basic necessities. If the goal is to serve more children, eligibility standards must better reflect the true cost of living families face today. At the same time, proposals that weaken quality standards and drastically reduce allowable administrative costs would undermine the very elements that make Head Start effective. Our agency is already grappling with a federally imposed $912,000 Head Start funding reduction that has forced painful cuts, including the loss of valued employees. It also reduced our available Head Start slots from 244 to 194. Further weakening the program through the proposed rule would jeopardize services for vulnerable children and families across rural communities like ours. We are grateful to Senator Schumer for his continued leadership in protecting Head Start and advocating for policies that strengthen, rather than diminish, opportunities for children and families,” said Renee M. Hungerford, Executive Director/CEO, Community Action of Orleans & Genesee. In Rochester , there are concerns that changes could compromise program quality and the well-being of families. Last year, Action for a Better Community enrolled 624 children in Head Start and Early Head Start programs. “As CEO of Action for a Better Community, I am in agreement with Senator Schumer and all other elected officials who oppose the proposed Head Start rule changes. Increasing class sizes, lowering teacher qualification standards, eliminating funding for essential medical screenings, and slashing allowable administrative costs from 15% to 5% would weaken a program that is foundational to children and families in Rochester. The current performance standards should be the floor for improvement, not the ceiling. We fully support strengthening Head Start, but never at the expense of program quality or the well being of the children and families we serve,” said Jerome H. Underwood, CCAP, President & CEO, Action for a Better Community. In Central New York , Head Start providers from Syracuse to Cortland are speaking out about the damage this proposed rule could inflict on everything from program operations, outcomes, and financial viability to the health, safety, and well-being of vulnerable children and families in local communities. Last year, the People’s Equal Action and Community Effort (PEACE) and the Cortland County Community Action Program (CAPCO) collectively served more than 1,000 Head Start and Early Head Start children and families across the region. “Like others, we have been closely following the proposed adjustments to Head Start Program Performance Standards. Our core criterion for evaluating reforms that streamline administrative processes is that fewer rules cannot mean fewer results. Head Start makes the same promise to every family: that their child will be safe, healthy, and ready for school - wherever they live. All reforms must align with that promise. Regulatory changes that affect performance standards or administrative expenses must not impede PEACE, Inc.'s ability to serve more than 918 Head Start children and families in the Central New York region. We appreciate Senator Schumer’s advocacy for Head Start, its mission, and its communities,” said Carolyn D. Brown, Executive Director, People’s Equal Action and Community Effort, Inc. “CAPCO stands firmly with Senator Schumer and our fellow Head Start agencies across NY State in opposition to the proposed Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs rule. A core strength of Head Start is that children and families, regardless of geography, are guaranteed access to a comprehensive and evidence-based model that addresses school readiness, health, nutrition, disabilities, and family well-being. If adopted, the proposed rule would significantly weaken federal standards that have long ensured consistent, high-quality Head Start and Early Head Start services nationwide, and that have long operated as essential safeguards for child health and safety, educational quality, and family support in Cortland County and across Central NY. Equally concerning, the proposed 5% administrative cost limit is unrealistically low for most, if not all, Head Start and Early Head Start grantees, including CAPCO. Imposing such a restrictive cap would force grantees to divert resources away from program governance, fiscal oversight, enrollment management, data systems, audit and reporting obligations, and other key infrastructure needed to operate high-quality Head Start programs. Rather than strengthening local programs, this approach would gradually erode agencies operational capacity, make compliance with federal requirements financially unsustainable for many, and ultimately risk dismantling the Head Start system through financial attrition. CAPCO is grateful to Senator Schumer for stepping up to fight for Head Start providers like us, and we join him in urging the Administration to preserve the strong federal performance standards that vulnerable children and families in our community depend upon,” said Greg Richards, Executive Director, Cortland County Community Action Program, Inc. In the Southern Tier , there are increasing concerns that the proposed changes may create unintended consequences for program quality, fiscal stability, workforce capacity, child and family access, and accountability. Last year, Pro Action of Steuben and Yates, Inc. enrolled 340 children and Opportunities for Otsego enrolled 229 children in Head Start programs. “Head Start is not simply a program—it is a promise to children and families that opportunity should not depend on income, geography, or circumstance. At Pro Action of Steuben and Yates, we see every day how Head Start and Early Head Start provide far more than early learning. These programs support school readiness, health and developmental screenings, nutrition, family engagement, and the stability parents need to work, learn, and build a stronger future for their children. While we support efforts to reduce unnecessary bureaucracy, that cannot come at the expense of the quality, safety, and comprehensive services that make Head Start effective. Proposals that increase class sizes, weaken staff qualification standards, reduce access to essential screenings and supports, or drastically limit allowable administrative costs would place significant strain on programs—especially in rural communities where families already face barriers related to transportation, workforce shortages, housing, and access to care. The current Head Start Program Performance Standards should be strengthened as a floor for quality, not lowered in a way that puts children and families at risk. We are grateful to Senator Schumer for his leadership, for listening to providers and families, and for standing up for the children, families, and communities who rely on Head Start. His willingness to engage on this issue matters deeply, and we appreciate his commitment to ensuring every child has the opportunity for a strong start,” said Laura Rossman, CEO / Executive Director of Pro Action of Steuben and Yates, Inc. “While Opportunities for Otsego supports efforts to reduce burdensome and duplicative regulations, it cannot come at the expense of providing quality early childhood education programming for the children and families we serve. The proposed Head Start Performance Standard revisions undermine the core components of comprehensive services that are the foundation of Head Start. The change in the allowable administrative costs, elimination of imperative dental and health requirements, lower teacher ratios coupled with increased class size, and changes to staff qualifications will significantly impact staff retention and the quality of services that we currently offer. The reality is that we transport families over 1.5 hours to get dental services due to lack of providers in our area, get children back on track with their immunization schedules, provide two thirds of a child’s nutrition while in program, provide necessary transportation to access services in our rural county, make referrals for early intervention services and work closely with school districts to transition those services when they enter kindergarten all while providing education with evidence based curriculum that is cross walked with the New York State education system. We are charged with serving the most vulnerable populations in a fiscally responsible and data driven way and the proposed revisions will devastate our ability to employ quality staff, continue to support families holistically, and will certainly impact outcomes of this valuable program that assists families and fosters success by giving them a head start. We applaud Senator Schumer’s efforts on this issue,” said Tanya Shalor, Chief Executive Officer of Opportunities for Otsego . In the Hudson Valley , there are concerns about larger class sizes, reducing staff qualification standards, and providing less federal support. Head Start of Rockland County services more than 1,000 children and families and aims to ensure they can continue delivering the support needed to help children in the community. “Head Start of Rockland, Inc. is deeply concerned about proposed changes to the Head Start Program Performance Standards including larger class sizes, reduced staff qualification standards, and a smaller administrative cap. The more than 1,000 children in Rockland County we serve should not receive a lesser standard of education, care, health, or safety because federal requirements change. We should be strengthening the standard for the next generation by investing in the systems, professionals, and services necessary to help children thrive—not lowering the expectations that will shape our communities and our nation for generations to come,” said Vernex Harding, Executive Director of the Head Start of Rockland. Schumer has long led the fight to protect Head Start in New York State. In the FY24 budget, when the Democrats held the Senate and as the then-Senate Majority Leader, Schumer secured a $275 million increase for Head Start, totaling $12.3 billion for Head Start. Earlier in the Trump administration, Schumer fought to ensure Head Start programs would receive payments amid the federal funding freeze so they could continue their essential services in rural and underserved communities. Schumer has also fought against the Trump administration’s efforts to eliminate Head Start altogether, illegally withhold the nearly $1 billion in federal funding for Head Start, and the decision to shutter the Region 2 Head Start Office serving more than 100,000 children and families across New York, New Jersey, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Additionally, Schumer secured an $85 million increase for Head Start, totaling $12.357 billion, in the most recent FY26 federal budget. ###

Major New Investment Upgrades Research Equipment And Modernizes Infrastructure To Support Next-Gen Aerospace Research Schumer Has Long History Of Supporting GE’s Growth And Boosting Upstate New York As Leader In Aerospace Technology Research Schumer: The Sky Is The Limit For Capital Region’s Workforce! Following his continued advocacy to boost Upstate New York as a leader in aerospace technology research and manufacturing, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today celebrated GE Aerospace’s $225 million investment in its Niskayuna facility, which is expected to create 75 new good-paying jobs over five years. Schumer explained that GE Aerospace will modernize the research facility, upgrading the Aerospace Research Center with new advanced research equipment and improved infrastructure needed to support the center’s cutting-edge work developing next-generation technological breakthroughs. “GE Aerospace’s new $225 million investment in Niskayuna, along with 75 high-skilled, good-paying jobs, shows the sky is the limit for our top-notch workforce. I have long supported GE Aerospace’s growth in Upstate New York and am thrilled that the workforce expansion of GE Aerospace Research in Niskayuna – and upgrades to the campus – are on their way to the Capital Region,” said Senator Schumer. “Investments like this are key to ensuring that cutting-edge aerospace technology research is happening at home in places like Schenectady County. I will keep fighting to support investments in the equipment we need to strengthen New York’s research and manufacturing leadership.” The planned $225 million investment will support research in AI, autonomy, robotics, advanced materials, future manufacturing, hypersonic propulsion, and hybrid electric flight. The Niskayuna campus has been a leader in technology development for more than 75 years and is driving innovation in aerospace technology research. The investment is projected to create 75 new good-paying jobs over the next five years, in addition to short-term construction jobs, and will also protect the jobs of scientists, engineers, researchers, and skilled laborers already employed at the facility. The facility will continue to support advanced technology projects, some funded by the federal government. Schumer added , “This investment is about building the future of aerospace—advancing cutting-edge research, bringing next-gen technologies to life, and creating 75 good-paying jobs. It’s an investment in the ideas and talent that will take aerospace innovation to new heights. I applaud GE Aerospace for its commitment to Upstate New York.” Schumer has a long history of supporting GE Vernova and GE Aerospace’s work in Upstate New York. In 2023, following his advocacy, Schumer announced that GE Vernova would create 200 new good-paying jobs, including skilled union operators and manufacturing engineers, while investing $50 million at its Schenectady, NY, facility to establish a new manufacturing line for its onshore wind business. In 2024, Schumer visited Unison, a GE Aerospace company, in Norwich to highlight over $3.4 million in local investment to modernize the plant, purchase new machines, and make major upgrades to the Southern Tier facility. In the Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) appropriations bill, Senator Schumer secured $40 million for GE Aerospace’s integrated hypersonic propulsion technology project with the Air Force, supporting the development and maturation of sensors and mission-critical future-of-flight technologies for the Air Force developed at GE Aerospace Research in Niskayuna, Unison in Norwich, and Innoveering in Bohemia. GE Aerospace is a leading provider of jet engines, components, and systems for commercial and military aircraft with a global service network to support these offerings. GE Aerospace and its joint ventures have an installed base of more than 44,000 commercial and 26,000 military aircraft engines, and the business is playing a vital role in shaping the future of flight. ###

In 2024, Tropical Storm Debby Devastated Communities Across The Southern Tier & Upstate New York, Schumer Says New Federal Funding Will Help Town Upgrade Roads & Critical Infrastructure Schumer Will Continue To Advocate For More Federal Investment To Ensure Town Has Resources Needed To Complete Project And Protect Local Taxpayers From Shouldering Crushing Costs of Storm Recovery Schumer: Fed $$ Puts Hamden On Road To Recovery! Following his advocacy , U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today announced $294,773.51 for the Town of Hamden to fund major repairs following Tropical Storm Debby. For nearly two years, the Town of Hamden has worked diligently with FEMA to advance its over $5 million request for disaster assistance and mitigation funding. Schumer said this grant is a key first step towards ensuring Hamden residents have the federal assistance they need to support critical repairs to their roads and mitigation efforts to protect the community from future flooding events. Schumer vowed to continue fighting to unlock the other federal support needed to rebuild and strengthen the community’s resilience. “I’m proud to deliver nearly $300,000 in federal funding needed for the Town of Hamden to repair roads damaged by Tropical Storm Debby. This investment will help restore safe and reliable roads for residents,” said Senator Schumer. “The community deserves to see these roads repaired without taxpayers having to shoulder the costs of storm recovery, and I’m proud to have helped make this first step a reality. I’ll keep fighting to deliver the remaining funding the Town needs to rebuild stronger and weather the storms ahead.” Schumer explained that because of flooding during the storm, the town saw severe damage along portions of Chamber Hollows Road, East Brook Road, and many other ditches and shoulders. Schumer said this funding will help keep the Town of Hamden and local taxpayers from bearing the costs of repair projects that were necessary for protecting the town’s infrastructure and local properties. These projects will address storm damage and make several improvements to enhance long-term resiliency. Work will replace existing metal pipes with properly sized concrete box culverts, along with new headwalls and wingwalls to provide additional structural support, improve drainage capacity, and meet New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) requirements. The project will also stabilize a failing roadside embankment where erosion has caused the bank to slide away from the roadway through the installation of soil nails. Additionally, the Town will restore damaged roadside ditches and shoulders in areas impacted by flooding, improving drainage, protecting roadways, and reducing the risk of future storm damage. Schumer’s August letter to FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton supporting federal funding for these repairs and improvements can be found HERE . Schumer said he will continue to fight for more federal funding to ensure the Town has the resources it needs to complete the full project. Schumer has been a long-standing fighter for Delaware County’s efforts to combat flood damage and natural disasters. After major storms in 2006 and 2011, Schumer advocated for federal disaster declarations on behalf of flood-impacted communities, including Delaware County, that would provide federal funding to enable places like Hamden and other communities within the county to recover and rebuild. As a result, local governments and thousands of property owners were able to apply for disaster assistance following these storms. In the aftermath of the 2006 flooding, Schumer successfully secured approval from FEMA to bring in temporary housing units for displaced residents, including those in Delaware County. In 2008, Schumer secured $300,000 in the Fiscal Year 2008 Appropriations Bill funding for flood protection measures in the Village of Sidney, which included infrastructure repairs to village pump stations and flap gates. With communities like Delaware County in mind, he helped author the provision in the Federal Disaster Aid Bill in 2012 that provided $200 million in Economic Development Administration (EDA) funding to help fund key economic growth projects in counties hammered by natural disasters. Schumer then secured $3.8 million from that provision for the Delaware County IDA. This funding provided critical support to relocate Amphenol Aerospace, keeping them in the community and saving over 950 jobs. Schumer's efforts to secure disaster declarations unlocked the FEMA Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (MPMG) fund, which brought nearly $7 million to local efforts to buy out over 100 flood-damaged properties in the Lower River Street neighborhood in Sidney for flood mitigation. In 2025, Schumer demanded that FEMA immediately reverse its decision to cancel federal funding for the Sidney Culvert Project , critical for mitigating flooding in the Village of Sidney, helping save lives, and reducing the damage and costs from flooding caused by extreme weather events. ###

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today applauded the finalization of the U.S. Commerce Department’s agreement to award up to $1 billion in federal CHIPS R&D funding, combined with an additional $1 billion in investment from IBM, to form a new entity to operate a secure 300mm quantum wafer fab at Albany NanoTech: “I’m thrilled that IBM has finalized and fully secured up to $1 billion in federal funding to launch a brand-new, cutting-edge quantum business in the Capital Region. Schumer explained that the Job Corps centers and programming help train tens of thousands of students across America each year, including thousands in New York, providing them with the skills they need to enter in-demand fields. “When the Trump administration announced that Job Corps was going to be eliminated, I got to work to protect it—traveling across Upstate New York to stand shoulder to shoulder with students, staff, and small businesses that have seen firsthand the benefits of this program. Last Year, Schumer Introduced And Led To Passage Bipartisan Legislation To Celebrate Historic Ice Hockey Game And Honor Olympic U.S. Men’s Ice Hockey Champions With Congressional Gold Medal Recognition – Including One To Be Displayed At New York’s Lake Placid Olympic Center Senator Reveals His Office Is Participating In Efforts to Explore Potential 2042 NYC-Lake Placid Bid To Have Highest Level Of Competition Featured At New York’s World-Class Facilities Schumer: Lake Placid Has A Rich Olympic History; We Should Look To Continue That Legacy! A year after the passage of his legislation honoring the 1980 U.S. Men’s Olympic Hockey Team with a Congressional Gold Medal , U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer last week visited Mt Van Hoevenberg Olympic Sports Complex to highlight efforts to bring the Winter Olympics back to the North Country. Schumer explained he is involved with new efforts to pursue a bid to host the 2042 Games and said there is no better place than New York State – with its rich sports history and world-class facilities – to host. “Lake Placid holds a long and special place in Winter Olympic history – having hosted both the 1932 and 1980 Games. Last year, I was proud to sponsor the commemoration of the 1980 ‘Miracle on Ice’ Olympic Ice Hockey Team with the Congressional Gold Medal to be displayed right here in Lake Placid. This historic team, made up of amateur players, sparked an explosion of American pride and patriotism when they defeated the vaunted Soviet Union Red Army Team at the 1980 Winter Olympic Games and then beat Finland in the gold medal game,” said Senator Schumer. “Lake Placid-NYC Games would mean the highest level of competition featured at our world-class facilities, including Lake Placid’s unique alpine and sliding infrastructure. I applaud Governor Hochul’s efforts to look at the feasibility of bringing the Games back here, and I am happy to lend my support to those exploratory efforts. The team defeated the mighty four-time Olympic champion Soviet Union Team in the semifinal game of the tournament and went on to win a gold medal in a thrilling come-from-behind game against the Finnish National Team. Schumer’s legislation celebrates the team’s historic victory with a Congressional Gold Medal to recognize their extraordinary achievement, including displaying one of the Congressional Gold Medals at the Lake Placid Olympic Center. Also, in 2016, Schumer visited the Olympic Training Center in Lake Placid to launch his successful effort to end the “Victory Tax” that had forced our medal-winning heroes to pay tax to the IRS on the value of their medals and accompanying victory stipends. Schumer says bringing the Olympics back to Lake Placid and New York would be a once-in-a-generation opportunity to use Lake Placid’s top-notch winter sports infrastructure and New York City’s iconic stadiums for a modern Olympic Games. New Fed Investment Secured By Schumer Will Rehabilitate Thousands Of Yards Of Pavement And Keep North Country Passengers Safe After Rule Change Ten Years Ago Rendered Piseco Airport Unable To Receive FAA Grant Funding For Repairs, Schumer Fought To Restore Piseco Airport’s Eligibility For Fed Infrastructure Funds Schumer: Piseco Airport Can Reach New Heights! After fighting to ensure the Piseco Airport would remain eligible for federal funding , U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today visited the Hamilton County airport and announced he has delivered $1,412,438 in federal funding through the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)’s Airport Improvement Program (AIP) to rehabilitate thousands of yards of pavement to ensure the airport is safe for North Country passengers. “Sometimes, people ask me why I visit all 62 counties, and this is exactly why. Ten years ago, on my trip to Hamilton County, my good friend Rick Wilt, who was Supervisor of Arietta, told me that the Town needed help with the FAA. Without annual aviation grant funding, there was simply no way the town could afford to operate and maintain its municipal airport. Now, Arietta is not only back in compliance, but I was proud to deliver $1.4 million in federal funding to help the airport invest in key safety upgrades,” said Senator Schumer. “Working with people like Rick to support New Yorkers in every corner of the state keeps me going. I was devastated to learn of Rick’s passing last month and extend my sincerest condolences to his family and friends, and all those who knew him. As we honor Rick and the community he loved, I’m here to say I will always fight to support Arietta and Hamilton County.” Schumer explained that there are six homes on eight properties lined immediately adjacent to the western side of the Piseco Airport along their airstrip, and that back in 1971, the Town of Arietta deeded homeowners perpetual access rights to the airstrip. However, Schumer explained, in 2013 the FAA established the Residential Through-the-Fence Access agreement, which said that any neighboring access to an airport must be sold at fair market value. As a result of the Piseco Airport’s non-compliance with this rule, the FAA prohibited Piseco from receiving grant funding through the Airport Improvement Program (AIP). According to Schumer, this crippled the ability of the Town of Arietta, with its population of 304, to maintain and operate its airport. Schumer fought to resolve the issue for the Town of Arietta and the Piseco Airport. In 2016, Supervisor Rick Wilt raised the issue during Schumer’s annual visit to Hamilton County. Schumer’s staff worked with the FAA to try to find a regulatory solution. Again in 2017, Schumer met with Town of Arietta and Hamilton County officials at the airport to discuss the issue in greater detail and pledged to include a policy fix in the next FAA Reauthorization Bill. In 2018, however, Schumer announced that a five-year FAA Reauthorization bill was signed into law, which included a legislative fix to the Residential Through-the-Fence Access, allowing certain airports, including the Piseco Airport, to be eligible to receive federal AIP funds through a grandfather clause. Since then, the airport has continued to receive its annual Airport Improvement Program grant funding of approximately $150,000, which it depends on in order to operate the municipally owned airfield. Just last month, Schumer delivered $1,412,438 in additional grant funding for key modernization upgrades. This grant funds the final phase, which consists of construction. This project rehabilitates 4,000 square feet of existing airport helipad to extend its useful life. This project also rehabilitates 10,500 square yards of existing Terminal Apron pavement to maintain the structural integrity of the pavement and to minimize foreign object debris. This federal funding was awarded through the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)’s Airport Improvement Program (AIP), which Schumer boosted in the Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law he led to passage in the Senate and the 2024 FAA reauthorization law. ###
