Schumer Called On NPS To Release Congressionally-Approved Funds When Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural National Historic Site Was The Last Site To Receive Annual Operating Budget Following his push , U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today released a statement announcing that the National Park Service (NPS) has released this year's annual federal funds for Buffalo’s Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site. Schumer said this funding is vital so the site can cover its bills, pay staff, and ensure the public can continue to access one of Western New York’s treasured historical sites. “The Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site holds a special place in the hearts of Buffalonians. That’s why, when I found out it was the only unit in the entire National Park System that had not received its funding, I called on the NPS to release it immediately. Today, I’m proud to announce that the NPS heeded my call and has released the funding,” said Senator Schumer. “As the home of the place where President Roosevelt took the oath of office to become our 26 th president, and where President McKinley tragically died, Buffalo plays a critical role in the story of a presidency that reshaped the country. As we celebrate America’s 250 th birthday this year, I will keep fighting to ensure New York’s rich history is accessible to the public for generations to come.” Earlier this month, Schumer called on the NPS to release the site’s funds without further delay and asked why this site was the only NPS site without its annual federal funding and what the NPS will do to ensure a delay like this never happens again. ###

Lawmakers Explain That, As We Prepare For Winter, It Is Important To Ensure Our Airports Have Infrastructure Needed To Keep Passengers And Equipment Safe Schumer Has Long History Of Delivering For Ithaca Tompkins International Airport, Providing Critical Fed Funding For Key Infrastructure Upgrades Including New Boarding Bridge, Snow Removal, Emergency Vehicles, High-Tech Baggage Screening System, And More Schumer: The Sky Is The Limit For Ithaca! U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, and U.S. Congressman Josh Riley today announced $6.5 million in federal funding for Ithaca Tompkins International Airport. Awarded through the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)’s Airport Improvement Program (AIP), which Schumer boosted in the Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, this federal investment will help the airport construct a new, 23,443-square-foot snow removal equipment facility to bring the airport up to current standards. “This $6.5+ million will help Ithaca Tompkins International Airport make much-needed upgrades to ensure safety in the winter by building a new snow removal equipment facility,” said Senator Schumer. “I fought hard to secure funding for airport improvement projects in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Investment & Jobs Law because I know how crucial it is to ensure the safety of our airports. As we prepare for winter, it is more important than ever to ensure our infrastructure can keep up with the needs of Ithacans, students, business leaders, and other travelers coming to and from Tompkins County. The sky is the limit for Ithaca!” “From big cities to rural communities, it is vital that New York’s airports have the resources they need to provide a safe and comfortable experience for all,” said Senator Gillibrand, ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Transportation Subcommittee. “I’m proud to deliver over $6.5 million in federal funding to build a new snow removal equipment facility at Ithaca Tompkins International Airport, and I’ll keep fighting to bring home the dollars that our airports need to offer first-rate service, operate efficiently, and ensure passenger safety.” “Upstate New Yorkers know winter doesn’t wait, and neither can the crews keeping our runways clear and passengers safe,” said Congressman Josh Riley. “The $6.5 million investment will help keep Ithaca Tompkins International Airport open and our region connected year-round. Safe, reliable air service is critical to growing our local economy. I’m proud to work with Senators Schumer and Gillibrand to bring those federal dollars back home to Tompkins County.” The lawmakers explained this federal funding will fund Phase 4 of the airport’s project to build a new snow equipment removal facility, which consists of building a foundation, structural elements, and the heating, ventilation, and air conditioning system. In FY2024, the Senators secured $1.5 million toward the construction of new emergency services facilities at Ithaca Tompkins International Airport. Schumer has long played a critical role in securing federal funding for key infrastructure upgrades, critical equipment, air service improvements, and passenger safety at Ithaca Tompkins International Airport. Previously, he successfully fought to secure millions of dollars in federal funding from the Department of Transportation for various projects at the airport including a new boarding bridge to accommodate the increased patronage of the airport, acquiring snow removal and emergency vehicles, and securing critical Small Community Air Service Development Program (SCASDP) funding to aid in the airport’s ability to market and promote new service options, ensuring their success. Senator Schumer also played a leading role in securing a new high - technology baggage screening system from the TSA that replaced the previously used manual bag-check system. Schumer visited Ithaca Tompkins Regional in February 2019 and called then-FAA Acting Administrator Daniel Elwell to fight for just under $10 million in critical FAA Airport Improvement Program (AIP) funding. As part of the Schumer-negotiated CARES Act, Schumer secured over $1.7 million for the airport, which was hit hard during the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2020, when United Airlines reduced services at ITH, he urged United to maintain current service levels to ITH , resulting in a reinstatement of routes post-pandemic, culminating in the successful push for a third daily flight to the D.C. metro area in 2025. ###

Last Year, Fort Drum Was Among Nine Sites Shortlisted For Army’s Next-Generation Nuclear Microreactor Program To Protect Domestic Military Bases From Grid Failures, Critical Energy Deficiencies, And Other Threats Fort Drum’s Strategic Mission Sets, Wheeler-Sack Army Airfield, Skilled Personnel, And Existing Infrastructure Make It The Best-In-Class To Demonstrate Safe And Secure, On-Site Nuclear Power Generation Schumer To Army: Fort Drum Needs Reliable Power To Protect National Security After the U.S. Army named Fort Drum as one of nine domestic Army installations under consideration to host the Janus Program, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today urged U.S. Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll to select Fort Drum for the Army’s effort to deploy a commercial nuclear microreactor to strengthen the installation’s energy resilience and support critical military operations. Schumer explained that the effort is to ensure military sites have secure, reliable power if the commercial power grid goes down and that after analyzing sites across the United States, including energy requirements and power infrastructure, that the Army shortlisted Fort Drum. “Fort Drum’s facilities, personnel, and infrastructure make it uniquely positioned to spearhead the Army’s Janus Program and demonstrate this important, innovative nuclear microreactor technology. Fort Drum is top-of-class to lead in advanced nuclear development. Bringing a safe and secure nuclear energy source to Fort Drum is a win-win for strengthening the base’s energy security and protecting our Army from vulnerabilities like grid failures,” said Senator Schumer. “As one of the most advanced and strategic military installations in the country, Fort Drum is ready, and the critical missions it carries out to protect our nation demand reliable, resilient, and independent onsite power generation.” The Department of the Army’s Janus Program is an initiative to deploy commercial nuclear microreactors on domestic military installations. The program will help strengthen the Army’s installation energy resilience, support future mission requirements, and advance next-generation nuclear energy. The program aims to have a working prototype operating on a domestic Army base by the end of 2028. Last year, the Army announced that nine military installations—including Fort Drum—were shortlisted for consideration to host a commercial nuclear microreactor under the Janus Program. Schumer explained that Fort Drum, home to Wheeler-Sack Army Airfield, which serves as the primary mobilization airfield for the 10 th Mountain Division, is one of the most strategic military installations in the United States. A nuclear microreactor would provide Fort Drum with a reliable, independent, and continuous source of energy for mission-critical support functions, command and control elements, mobilization activities, and other vital capabilities, including during grid-level energy infrastructure outages and the disruption of key power supplies. Schumer added that Fort Drum’s location would allow the Army to assess a microreactor’s performance under harsh weather and other conditions needed to inform its efforts to integrate energy solutions into future operations. Schumer also explained Fort Drum currently uses over 60 megawatts of power, most of which is pulled from the local grid. Fort Drum is a vital economic and community anchor for the North Country, supporting thousands of military and civilian jobs. Schumer underscored that Fort Drum is well-equipped to demonstrate how nuclear power can reduce vulnerabilities and reinforce critical U.S. defense infrastructure. It is expected that the commercial microreactor would not require significant land use changes and would be designed to produce up to 20 megawatts (MW) of power to support installation operations. Fort Drum officials and the local community have conveyed support for the site’s selection for the Janus Program. Schumer’s letter to U.S. Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll can be found HERE or below: Dear Secretary Driscoll: Late last year, the U.S. Army announced a list of nine domestic military installations—including Fort Drum, New York—to be considered for the deployment of a commercial nuclear microreactor under the Army’s Janus Program. The Janus Program is a critical opportunity to strengthen the Total Army’s installation energy resilience through the deployment of next-generation nuclear energy and support future mission requirements consistent with the goals of the National Defense Strategy. I write to encourage you to select Fort Drum, given the installation’s distinct combination of operational need, personnel, and existing infrastructure that make it an optimal site to spearhead the Janus Program. Fort Drum is one of the most advanced and strategic military installations in the United States. Fort Drum has the facilities, personnel, and infrastructure needed to be the best-in-class site to field a nuclear microreactor. The garrison is home to Wheeler-Sack Army Airfield, which serves as the primary mobilization airfield for the 10th Mountain Division and is a strategic asset and power projection capability for the Joint Force. Moreover, Fort Drum and the 10th Mountain Division’s operational tempo and strategic importance make the installation the ideal candidate to demonstrate the need for secure, onsite power generation to support military installations and critical mission sets. As the Army continues to prepare for large-scale combat operations (LSCO) and conflicts in increasingly contested environments, where adversaries will target critical infrastructure, including the potential disruption of highly interconnected key power supplies and grid-level energy infrastructure, military installations must be capable of executing their mission even during prolonged outages and disruptions to the local grid. A nuclear microreactor would provide Fort Drum with a reliable, non-carbon polluting, independent, and continuous source of energy for mission-critical support functions, command and control elements, mobilization activities, and other vital capabilities during contingency operations. It would also allow the Army to validate the operational benefits of advanced nuclear energy while strengthening the resilience of one of its premier power projection platforms. Furthermore, serving as the home to the 10th Mountain Division—the most deployed conventional Army unit since 2001—Fort Drum has long been a leader in developing, testing, and proving the Army’s cold-weather and expeditionary capabilities, including hosting large-scale training exercises for multi-domain operations in harsh climate and austere environments that simulate conditions warfighters may encounter downrange. Fort Drum’s permissive training environment would allow the Army to assess a microreactor’s performance under realistic operational conditions, enhance the installation’s energy resilience by reducing grid dependency vulnerabilities and interdependencies, and strengthen the Army’s ability to maintain a high readiness posture, including by informing its efforts to integrate resilient energy solutions into future operations. For these reasons, I urge you to select Fort Drum to host a nuclear microreactor as part of the Army’s Janus Program. I appreciate the careful consideration you will give Fort Drum’s candidacy during the site selection process, and I am confident you will find that Fort Drum has the personnel, infrastructure, resources, and capacity consistent with the Army’s basing criteria under the Janus Program. ###

West Park Post Office Has Served Ulster County Community For More Than 130 Years Until USPS Abruptly Announced Its Closure, Forcing Customers To Travel Five Miles Away To Highland To Collect Mail Instead Schumer Urges USPS To Restore Postal Operations So Residents And Small Businesses Can Easily Receive Medications, Checks & Bills, Packages, And Other Important Mail Schumer To USPS: West Park Deserves A Post Office In West Park After the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) announced its plan to close the West Park Post Office , and then officially closed the facility on July 24, impacting approximately 170 post office box holders, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer called on the USPS to immediately restore the post office and work with the community to avoid disruptions to reliable mail service. For years, Schumer has fought relentlessly to protect post offices across Upstate New York, demanding accountability from the U.S. Postal Service, ensuring rural residents have a voice in decisions that affect them, and defending the local institutions that keep small communities connected. “The West Park Post Office is more than a place where residents pick up mail and drop off packages; it’s the center of the community. The abrupt closure of this office, now forcing residents and small businesses to drive miles away to pick up medications, packages, and other important mail, is simply unacceptable,” said Senator Schumer. “Every day this post office remains closed is another day this community is without an essential asset it depends on. West Park deserves a post office in West Park, and that’s why I’m calling on the USPS to work with the community to reopen it immediately.” "The West Park Post Office has been an important part of our hamlet for generations, providing essential services while serving as a place that connects neighbors and strengthens our community. On behalf of the Town of Esopus, I want to thank Senator Schumer for his continued support and for standing up for the residents of West Park and our entire community toward a solution that restores reliable postal service close to home," said Roscoe T. Pecora, Town Supervisor, Town of Esopus. Earlier this year, the USPS announced its plan to close the West Park Post Office, forcing approximately 170 post office box holders to travel five miles away to Highland to collect their mail. The West Park community has rallied against the closure of its gathering place, emphasizing that residents and small businesses depend on the post office for medications, checks, bills, packages, and more. The USPS has not provided any updates to the local community, including the details of a new lease or a timeline for the potential reopening. Schumer said the USPS must work with local stakeholders to restore this essential public service for the West Park community. Schumer’s letter to USPS Postmaster General David Steiner can be found HERE or below: Dear Postmaster General Steiner, I write with concern regarding the future of the West Park Post Office, located at 1740 US-9W, West Park, NY 12493. On July 24, 2026, the United States Postal Service (USPS) issued a temporary closure of the West Park Post Office, citing a loss of lease. Since then, USPS has provided no timeline or concrete plans to restore postal operations in West Park and to ensure that the community’s post office remains in West Park. I urge you to act swiftly and diligently to reinstate the post office in West Park, and to work transparently and collaboratively with community stakeholders in that process. While I appreciate that the Postal Service has provided alternative mail services for West Park residents at the neighboring Highland Post Office, this location is more than five miles away for many residents, postal workers, and small business owners. West Park is a rural community and any disruptions to mail operations pose serious challenges for many of the residents and small businesses who depend on the Postal Service in their daily lives and who will now have to drive to another town to pick up their medications, checks and bills, packages, and other important mail. Furthermore, in West Park, the post office is not just a place where residents pick up their mail and drop off their packages. The West Park Post Office is the heart and center of the town – it is the place where residents build close-knit connections with their neighbors and postal workers, and where they see West Park’s identity represented in a community space. The closure of West Park Post Office is a real detriment to the community and any further delays in reinstating the West Park Post Office are unacceptable. Therefore, I urge the Postal Service to immediately act to reinstate the West Park Post Office. Again, I also urge the Postal Service to transparently engage with West Park residents and establish a clear plan to restore the West Park Post Office as quickly as possible. Thank you for your attention to this important matter. I look forward to your response. ###

Schumer’s CHIPS & Science Law Has Delivered Hundreds Of Billions In New Investment To Bring Back American Manufacturing, Strengthen Supply Chains, & Create Good-Paying Jobs Upstate New York Is Building The Critical Technologies The World Needs—Ensuring The U.S. Leads The Future, Not China Schumer: Upstate NY Is Powering America’s Chip Comeback Four years after his landmark CHIPS & Science Act was signed into law, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer marked the anniversary by highlighting how Upstate New York communities that made America a manufacturing powerhouse throughout the nation’s history are now powering the nation’s semiconductor comeback, attracting billions of dollars of investment, and delivering tens of thousands of new, good-paying jobs across Upstate NY. From IBM in Endicott, which helped define the modern computing era, to General Electric in Schenectady and Syracuse, birthplace of some of America’s most important innovations, to Kodak in Rochester, which pioneered imaging technologies used around the globe, Upstate New York discovered, developed, and built technologies that transformed the world. Schumer said decades of disinvestment, offshoring, and the decline of major legacy manufacturers left too many communities in Upstate New York struggling to replace the family-supporting careers and opportunities that once defined them. As advanced manufacturing moved overseas, America became increasingly dependent on foreign supply chains for the semiconductors that power everything from smartphones and cars to defense technologies and artificial intelligence. Schumer said his bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law was designed to change that by leveling the playing field and giving the communities that once powered the country’s industrial past a real chance to build America’s technological future. “For too long, America watched manufacturing move overseas, weakening our supply chains and leaving Upstate communities behind. That’s why I fought to pass my CHIPS & Science Act into Law with Upstate New York as my north star—because I knew the communities that powered America’s industrial past could be the ones to build its future,” said Senator Schumer. “Four years later, we are seeing the full promise of this law: rebuilding America’s semiconductor industry from the ground up, bringing manufacturing back, strengthening the critical supply chains we depend on, and creating pathways to tens of thousands of good-paying careers for the next generation of Upstate New Yorkers. We’re proving that America can once again make the technologies the world needs and lead the industries of the future—and outcompete China.” Schumer said he crafted the CHIPS & Science Law with Upstate New York as his north star because he believed the state had what America needed to lead the next generation of innovation: renowned research institutions, a deep legacy of advanced manufacturing, water and power infrastructure and sites primed for investment, world-class workers, and communities with generations of experience building the technologies that changed the world. Schumer said Upstate New York has the foundation the United States needs to win a global tech race that the country cannot afford to lose. Schumer said investments spurred by his CHIPS & Science Law are already ushering in an economic renaissance across Upstate New York. In four years, Schumer’s bipartisan legislation has delivered a significant resurgence in cutting-edge research, manufacturing, supply chain investment, and workforce development programs across Upstate New York. “By the end of the decade, it is estimated that one in four U.S.-made chips will be produced within 350 miles of Upstate New York’s Semiconductor Superhighway—more than any other region in the country,” said Schumer . “This will be a stunning manufacturing renaissance in a region that was in a long and seemingly intractable decline, bleeding its population and stymying its potential to contribute to America’s economic preeminence. When Carrier left Syracuse and moved operations to Singapore and China, taking away so many good-paying jobs, I was angry—I still am. But that’s when I knew we needed to stop pining wistfully about the ‘Glory Days’ of years past and make it my mission to rebuild our industrial base and reinvest in the communities that built America. Today, because of my CHIPS and Science Law, Upstate New York is beaming and boasting that the ‘Best is Yet to Come.’ Optimism, confidence, a growing population, home appreciation, and jobs-jobs-jobs. Having a chance to achieve this dream is what the CHIPS and Science Law is all about.” BRINGING AMERICAN MANUFACTURING BACK Schumer said his CHIPS & Science Law is delivering historic investments that are positioning Upstate New York at the center of America’s semiconductor comeback. In Central New York , Micron has broken ground and poured concrete for the first fab of its historic $100+ billion memory chip manufacturing complex, supported by a $6.1 billion CHIPS direct funding award combined with billions more in incentives through the federal semiconductor Investment Tax Credit. The project represents one of the largest private investments in American history and will create tens of thousands of jobs across the region. In the Capital Region , Schumer has secured more than $2 billion in federal CHIPS funding to support GlobalFoundries’ continued growth. Schumer also delivered $1 billion in federal CHIPS R&D funding , combined with an additional $1 billion investment from IBM, to support a next-generation quantum wafer fab at Albany NanoTech and strengthen Upstate New York’s role as a global leader in semiconductor research. Together, GlobalFoundries, IBM, and NY Creates anchor a world-class ecosystem in the Capital Region. These investments are ensuring that the most advanced chip technologies are designed, developed, and manufactured in America. By the end of the decade, it is estimated that one in four U.S.-made chips will be produced within 350 miles of Upstate New York —more than any other region in the country. Schumer said this is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to further solidify Upstate New York’s prominence as a critical hub for the research, development, and manufacturing of these technologies. REBUILDING CRITICAL SUPPLY CHAINS Schumer said the resurgence of domestic manufacturing requires more than just chip factories but also materials, equipment, and other small businesses. Schumer said major investments are fueling new opportunities for other small and mid-sized manufacturers, contractors, and suppliers, helping build a stronger, more secure domestic supply chain. In Western New York , Edwards Vacuum is nearing completion of a first-of-its-kind $300+ million dry pump manufacturing facility, supported by $18 million in CHIPS funding, to produce vacuum technology used in manufacturing next-gen chips. In Central New York , TTM Technologies opened a new advanced printed circuit board manufacturing facility in Onondaga County, made possible by a $30 million federal investment Schumer delivered, which will create 400 good-paying jobs and strengthen domestic semiconductor and defense manufacturing supply chains. In the Southern Tier , Menlo Micro will invest $50 million to build a microchip switch manufacturing facility in Tompkins County, creating 100 new jobs. In the North Country , Corning Incorporated finalized a $32 million agreement supporting a $315 million investment to increase production of specialized glass. Schumer also secured a federal Tech Hub designation created by his CHIPS & Science Law for the Syracuse-Rochester-Buffalo region to become a Semiconductor Superhighway, delivering $40 million in federal investment for workforce training, commercialization, and supply chain initiatives to support the chip industry’s buildout across Upstate New York. To date, $2.1 million has been awarded across the NY SMART I-Corridor helping hundreds of companies support growth in semiconductor supply chains. “The CHIPS and Science Act is giving Upstate New York the opportunity to do what no single community could accomplish alone. By working together with our partners across Buffalo, Rochester, and Syracuse, we are creating opportunities for local businesses to grow and for people to build good careers in the semiconductor industry. This work is delivering lasting economic change and advancing America’s innovation, security, and economic strength,” said Grant Loomis, President & CEO of the Buffalo Niagara Partnership . BUILDING THE FUTURE WORKFORCE From cleanrooms to classrooms, Schumer’s law has laid the foundation for a stronger workforce by investing in science-based research, institutions of higher education, and workforce programs that prepare people for good-paying technology, construction, and manufacturing jobs across Upstate New York. In July, Schumer announced the University of Rochester-led STELLAR Engine was selected for a $15 million award through the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF)’s Regional Innovation Engines Program, created by the CHIPS & Science Law, to supercharge laser technologies' growth across the Rochester-Finger Lakes region. In March, Schumer also announced that Binghamton University-led New Energy New York (NENY) was selected as an awardee for the second phase of the NSF’s Regional Innovation Engines Program, bringing up to $45 million over the next 3 years for Binghamton’s groundbreaking battery hub. This investment builds on Schumer’s extensive legacy of delivering for Binghamton, including a prestigious Tech Hubs designation in 2023 and over $113 million in public investment in 2022, for the Southern Tier to become the next battery tech hub. Schumer said Upstate New York’s semiconductor superhighway and innovation ecosystem will only succeed by training the workers who will build, operate, and sustain these advanced facilities, including engineers, researchers, machinists, welders, electricians, plumbers, and more. In Central New York , according to UA Local 81 assessments, approximately 2,000 plumbers and steamfitters will be required on site daily during the five-year construction period of the Micron facility, demonstrating the unprecedented opportunity for growth the semiconductor boom is creating for Upstate New York’s building and construction trades. Furthermore, IBEW Local 43 recently invested $7 million to expand its training center and apprenticeship pipeline due to the skyrocketing demand for electricians spurred by Micron and other projects across the region. Upstate New Yorkers like Morghan White showcase how the investments fueled by the CHIPS & Science Law are creating new pathways to good-paying careers. After returning to Central New York , Morghan entered an apprenticeship through UA Local 81 and is building a career in the skilled trades. In Western New York , Anthony Cercone , a graduate of the Advanced Manufacturing and Engineering program at Orleans/Niagara BOCES, recently began as a manufacturing engineer at Edwards Vacuum’s new facility. In the Southern Tier , Schumer has supported Ithaca Area Economic Development’s Tompkins Build industry-led pre-apprenticeship program, which connects residents with pathways into registered apprenticeships through partnerships with 10 participating unions. And, at Binghamton University, Schumer secured $1 million in federal funding for a state-of-the-art microelectronics packaging cleanroom that will help train more than 100 students each year for critical microelectronics and semiconductor manufacturing jobs. Together, these stories show the promise Schumer envisioned and delivered: bringing manufacturing back, strengthening critical supply chains, and creating pathways to good-paying jobs for thousands of Upstate New Yorkers. Four years after his bipartisan bill became law, the CHIPS & Science Law is giving Upstate New Yorkers an opportunity to once again build the technologies that will power America’s future—just as they have done for generations. ###

In 2024, Tropical Storm Debby Devastated Communities Across The Southern Tier & Upstate New York, Schumer Says Federal Funding Will Help Town Address Debby’s Damage To Roads & Critical Infrastructure Schumer Previously Advocated For Federal Disaster Declarations To Help Delaware County And Protect Local Taxpayers In Communities Like Hamden From The Crushing Costs of Storm Recovery Schumer To FEMA: Help Hamden Rebuild And Weather The Storms Ahead Today, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer called on the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to cut through the red tape and stop delays to help the Town of Hamden in Delaware County complete the recovery, repair, and mitigation efforts the town was forced to undertake following the remnants of Tropical Storm Debby. For nearly two years, the Town of Hamden has worked diligently with FEMA to advance its over $5,000,000 request for disaster assistance and mitigation funding. However, bureaucratic delays and staff turnover at FEMA have kept Hamden residents waiting for federal assistance to support critical repairs to their roads and mitigation efforts to protect the community from future flooding events. “The Town of Hamden has been on a long road to recovery. It’s time for FEMA to put the pedal to the metal and help this community get back on track after the damage and devastation caused by the remnants of Tropical Storm Debby,” said Senator Schumer. “FEMA must move quickly to review and approve the federal assistance Hamden needs to rebuild its roads and ensure its infrastructure is ready to weather the storms ahead. I’ll keep fighting to bring federal resources to Delaware County and shield local taxpayers from the crushing costs of storm recovery.” Schumer explained that because of flooding during the storm, the town saw severe damage along portions of Chamber Hollows Road, East Brook Road, and many other ditches and shoulders. Schumer said approving this funding would help keep the Town of Hamden and local taxpayers from shouldering the costs of repair projects that were necessary for protecting the town’s infrastructure and local properties. These projects will address storm damage and make several improvements to enhance long-term resiliency. Work will replace existing metal pipes with properly sized concrete box culverts, along with new headwalls and wingwalls to provide additional structural support, improve drainage capacity, and meet New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) requirements. The project will also stabilize a failing roadside embankment where erosion has caused the bank to slide away from the roadway through the installation of soil nails. Additionally, the Town will restore damaged roadside ditches and shoulders in areas impacted by flooding, improving drainage, protecting roadways, and reducing the risk of future storm damage. If approved at the proposed 75% federal cost-share, federal investment from FEMA will cover $5,032,655 of the project cost. Town of Hamden Supervisor Wayne Marshfield said, “The Town of Hamden is currently seeking vital financial assistance from FEMA in the amount of $5,032,655 for the August 2024 flooding disaster. With an annual Town of Hamden Highway Department budget of just over one million dollars, we do not have the finances to fund this without the critical FEMA funding. FEMA funding is crucial to us maintaining a safe and reliable infrastructure for our community.” Schumer has been a long-standing fighter for Delaware County’s efforts to combat flood damage and natural disasters. After major storms in 2006 and 2011, Schumer advocated for federal disaster declarations on behalf of flood-impacted communities, including Delaware County, that would provide federal funding to enable places like Hamden and other communities within the county to recover and rebuild. As a result, local governments and thousands of property owners were able to apply for disaster assistance following these storms. In the aftermath of the 2006 flooding, Schumer successfully secured approval from FEMA to bring in temporary housing units for displaced residents, including those in Delaware County. In 2008, Schumer secured $300,000 in the Fiscal Year 2008 Appropriations Bill funding for flood protection measures in the Village of Sidney, which included infrastructure repairs to village pump stations and flap gates. With communities like Delaware County in mind, he helped author the provision in the Federal Disaster Aid Bill in 2012 that provided $200 million in Economic Development Administration (EDA) funding to help fund key economic growth projects in counties hammered by natural disasters. Schumer then secured $3.8 million from that provision for the Delaware County IDA. This funding provided critical support to relocate Amphenol Aerospace, keeping them in the community and saving over 950 jobs. Schumer's efforts to secure disaster declarations unlocked the FEMA Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (MPMG) fund, which brought nearly $7 million to local efforts to buy out over 100 flood-damaged properties in the Lower River Street neighborhood in Sidney for flood mitigation. In 2025, Schumer demanded FEMA immediately reverse its decision to cancel federal funding for the Sidney Culvert Project , critical for mitigating flooding in the Village of Sidney, helping save lives, and reducing the damage and costs from flooding caused by extreme weather events. A copy of Senator Schumer’s letter to FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton can be found HERE or below: Dear Administrator Hamilton, I write to urge the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to swiftly approve the Town of Hamden’s federal disaster reimbursements under Project Worksheets #796462, #811378, #811378, #811380, #811384, #811386, #811388 (DR-4825-NY). The Town of Hamden is awaiting final approval for over $5,000,000 in funding to repair and improve the resilience of Chamber Hollows Road, East Brook Road, and Oxbow Hollow Road, as well as ditches and shoulder areas that experienced significant damage due to flooding in 2024 from the remnants of Tropical Storm Debby. In August of 2024, the remnants of Tropical Strom Debby brought heavy rain and flooding to communities across New York’s Southern Tier, including the Town of Hamden in Delaware County. The Town began working with FEMA and New York State Department of Homeland Security and Emergency Services (NYS DHSES) in 2024 to utilize federal funding to help pay for cleanup, repairs, and remediation from these flood event damages. It has worked diligently over the past two years to comply with multiple requests for information so that FEMA would approve and agree to reimburse the project costs of $5,032,655. These critical improvements will address storm damage and enhance long-term resiliency. Work will replace existing metal pipes with properly sized concrete box culverts, along with new headwalls and wingwalls to provide additional structural support, improve drainage capacity, and meet New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) requirements. The project will also stabilize a failing roadside embankment through the installation of soil nails. Additionally, the Town will restore damaged roadside ditches and shoulders impacted by flooding, improving drainage, protecting roadways, and reducing the risk of future storm damage. The annual Town of Hamden Highway Department budget is set at just over one million dollars, leaving the municipality without the finances to complete these critical repair and mitigation projects without FEMA assistance, putting their infrastructure, property, and community at risk. It will be two years this August since the flooding rains and storm took place. The community has been extremely patient in waiting for necessary repair work and the Town remains vulnerable to further damage should another storm occur before repairs are completed. Given the importance of these projects, I ask that you promptly review the applications and swiftly approve the projects to free up the necessary funding that will enable the Town of Hamden to fully recover from the destruction of Tropical Strom Debby and better prepare for the next storm. Thank you in advance for your consideration of this important request. I look forward to hearing from you. ###

Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural National Historic Site – Where Then-Vice President Theodore Roosevelt Took The Oath Of Office To Become America’s 26 th President – Needs Annual Congressionally-Approved Funds to Pay Bills And Staff Schumer Says: As We Celebrate America’s 250 th Birthday, We Must Ensure This Treasured Buffalo Historical Site Remains Accessible To The Public Schumer To NPS: Release Annual Funds For Vital Site For This Jewel Of American History Here In Western NY U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today called on the National Park Service (NPS) to release this year's funds for Buffalo’s Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site. The site, which is a National Historic Site, says it is the only unit in the entire National Park System that has not received its congressionally appropriated FY26 operating funds. With the end of the fiscal year quickly approaching at the end of September, the site’s leadership says it needs these funds to cover its bills, pay staff, and ensure the public can continue to access one of Western New York’s treasured historical sites. Schumer called on the NPS to immediately release the site’s funds and explain why this site has been the last left without funding this far into the fiscal year. “As a place of tragedy and the transition of presidential power, the Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site holds a special place in the hearts of Buffalonians and the nation. As the place where the assassinated President McKinley tragically passed away, and President Roosevelt took the oath of office to become our 26 th president, this home tells the story of the origins of a presidency that reshaped the country,” said Senator Schumer. “The site relies on federal funding to cover its bills and pay staff, but its leadership says it is the only unit in the entire National Park System that has not received its allocated federal funding. That makes no sense and is unacceptable. As we celebrate America’s 250 th birthday, it’s more important than ever to preserve our country’s rich history. That’s why I’m calling on the NPS to immediately release the congressionally appropriated support needed to keep this historic house’s doors open so Americans can continue to access one of New York’s, and the nation’s, treasured historical sites.” The Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural National Historic Site is the house where, on September 14, 1901, Theodore Roosevelt took the oath of office following the assassination of President William McKinley, becoming the 26th President of the United States. Thanks to decades of local activism and preservation work, the house has been preserved for generations and now operates as a unit of the National Park System. The Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural National Historic Site relies on Congressionally appropriated funds for approximately one-third of its operating budget. The delay of its allocated funds has postponed the completion of essential work, including replacement of a 16-year-old HVAC system and repairs to the building's historic Victorian roof. These upgrades are desperately needed to ensure the aging building’s integrity and to continue providing the optimal visitor and staff experience at the site. Schumer said the NPS must release the site’s funds without further delay and asked why this site is the only NPS site without its annual federal funding and what the NPS will do to ensure a delay like this never happens again. Schumer’s letter to Acting National Park Service Director Jessica Bowron can be found HERE or below: Dear Acting Director Bowron, I write to urge the immediate release of Fiscal Year 2026 operating funds to the Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural National Historic Site in Buffalo, New York. According to Site Superintendent Spencer Morgan, this site is now the only unit in the entire National Park System that has not received its congressionally appropriated FY26 operating funds with the end of the fiscal year fast approaching. If the site does not receive these funds by the end of September, it risks being unable to cover its bills and meet payroll, threatening not only the continued operation of the site and employment of the staff, but also public access to one of New York’s, and the nation’s, treasured historical sites. As a place of tragedy and the transition of presidential power, the Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site holds a special place in the hearts of Buffalonians, the nation, and Roosevelt history buffs alike. It is the house where, on September 14, 1901, Theodore Roosevelt took the oath of office following the tragic assassination of President William McKinley, becoming the 26th President of the United States. It stands today, preserved for generations since Roosevelt’s tenure, thanks to decades of local activism and preservation work. It now operates as a unit of the National Park System as a testament to a pivotal moment and person in our nation's history. This site is not only one of great historic significance, but it also provides meaningful, ongoing value to the Buffalo community. It attracts visitors from far and wide – boosting the local economy, offering free field trips for local students, and educating the public on the origins of a presidency that reshaped the country. The site relies on the National Park Service for roughly a third of its operating budget, and the prolonged delay in receiving its promised FY26 funds has delayed the completion of essential work, including replacement of a 16-year-old HVAC system and repairs to the building's historic Victorian roof. These upgrades are desperately needed to ensure the aging building’s integrity and to continue providing the optimal visitor and staff experience at the site. Reports suggest that National Park Service maintenance funds have been redirected to support America250 celebrations in Washington, D.C. While our nation’s semi-quincentennial is an important milestone to honor, it must not come at the expense of the continued maintenance, preservation, and operation of our many other historic sites and protected places across the country. In Buffalo, the Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site cannot meet payroll or complete vital maintenance and preservation projects without its congressionally appropriated FY26 funds. I therefore urge the National Park Service to release the site's FY26 operating funds without further delay, and request that you provide my office with a clear timeline for disbursement. I would also appreciate an explanation of why this site, alone among all National Park Service units nationwide, has been left without its funding this far into the fiscal year, and what steps the agency is taking to ensure this does not happen again. The Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site belongs to every American as a piece of our shared history. It deserves the timely support Congress has provided for it, especially as America celebrates our 250th anniversary. Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent matter. I look forward to your response. ###

Today, U.S. Senators Charles Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand called on Congress to quickly pass legislation renaming a Buffalo, New York post office in honor of Buffalo native William J. Donovan, known as the “Father of American Intelligence.” The bill, H.R. 1706, would designate the U.S. Postal Service facility at 1200 William Street as the William J. Donovan Post Office Building. Donovan was a World War I and World War II hero, a Medal of Honor recipient, and a longtime public servant who helped position the U.S. as a global leader in national security as founding director of the Office of Strategic Services (OSS). In a letter to Rand Paul, chairman of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, and Ranking Member Gary Peters, Gillibrand and Schumer wrote that the renaming would be a fitting tribute to a leader who dedicated his life to national and local service. "William J. Donovan served our nation with honor and dedication," said Senator Gillibrand. "He defended our country during both world wars, received the Medal of Honor for his bravery, and helped position the United States as a leader in national security. Renaming the post office in his honor will help his incredible legacy endure in Western New York." “‘Wild Bill’ Donovan is an American hero who received the Medal of Honor and also was a founder of the modern intelligence community. He dedicated his life to serving Western New York and our country and played a key role protecting our national security during both world wars and in the decades after,” said Senator Schumer. “I cannot think of any better way to honor his legacy than with a Buffalo post office designation.” In 1923, Donovan received the Medal of Honor for his actions during a 1918 battle near Landres-et-Saint-Georges, France, where he was shot but refused to leave the battlefield. He later served as U.S. attorney for the Western District of New York and as an assistant attorney general under President Calvin Coolidge. During World War II, Donovan founded and directed the Office of Strategic Services, the precursor to the modern-day Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). He retired from military service as a major general. If approved by the committee, the bill moves to the full Senate for consideration. Full text of the bill can be found here . ###

Schumer Leads Bipartisan Push To Apple CEO Tim Cook Urging Company Not To Use Chinese Memory Chips, Which Would Undermine American Workers And The Nation’s Growing Domestic Memory Chip Industry – Including In Central NY Schumer Warns Apple Purchasing Chinese-Made Memory Chips Would Hurt America’s National Security And Shape Memory Chip Market By Setting Dangerous Example For Other Companies To Follow Schumer To Apple: Don’t Undermine American Workers, Manufacturing, And National Security By Using Chinese Military-Linked Memory Chips Today, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer led a bipartisan group of Senate colleagues calling on Apple CEO Tim Cook to commit that no memory chips produced by Chinese military-linked companies ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) or Yangtze Memory Technologies Co (YMTC) will be used in any Apple product sold anywhere in the world. Schumer explained that communities across Upstate New York, including Central New York, are growing centers for some of the country’s most advanced chip manufacturing, and that this would hurt the nation’s domestic semiconductor supply chain by setting a dangerous precedent for other companies to follow. “Using Chinese-made chips produced by companies allied with the Chinese Communist Party regime undermines American manufacturing and national security,” said Schumer. Schumer also demanded answers about Apple’s reported testing of Chinese memory chips and its alleged efforts to lobby the Trump administration against national security restrictions on Chinese semiconductor suppliers. “Fueled by investment from my Chips & Science Law, workers in Central New York and across the country are carrying out the largest domestic expansion of domestic memory chip production in a generation, and American companies, like Apple, should be buying chips stamped ‘Made in America,’ not from companies linked to the Chinese military,” said Senator Schumer. “I wrote my CHIPS & Science Law, so we would make American microchips again, with American workers, and not be over-reliant on semiconductors from overseas. That’s why I’m leading a bipartisan group of senators calling on Apple CEO Tim Cook to commit to not using memory chips produced by Chinese military-linked companies. I’ve long sounded the alarm on the grave national security and economic threats posed by YMTC, CMXT, and other companies backed by the Chinese Communist Party. Apple integrating these Chinese chips into its supply chain would send a dangerous message to other American companies that they, too, should turn to Chinese-made chips. This, despite the real national security concerns and how the CCP is actively trying to undermine American chip manufacturing companies by propping up Chinese companies like CXMT and YMTC, I will always fight to protect Upstate New York’s growing semiconductor superhighway, which is key to our economy and national security.” In the letter , Schumer and colleagues warn that the Department of Defense has designated both CXMT and YMTC as Chinese military companies and that federal law already requires the U.S. government to phase products containing their semiconductors out of federal procurement, a law that exists after a Schumer-led effort to include this requirement in the FY2023 National Defense Authorization Act. The senators argue that Apple’s adoption of Chinese memory chips for use anywhere in its supply chain would undermine American semiconductor manufacturing, strengthen Beijing’s military-industrial base, and send a market signal that could steer the global technology industry toward suppliers the U.S. government has identified as national security threats. Schumer has long fought to stop the growth of Chinese chipmakers with ties to the Chinese Communist Party and its military ambitions that threaten U.S. national security. In addition to his successful inclusion of a provision in the FY2023 NDAA to remove Chinese-made chips from the defense supply chain, Schumer also successfully advocated in 2022 for the Biden administration to add YMTC and dozens of other Chinese companies to a trade blacklist, restricting U.S. exports of advanced U.S. technology that could be used by these companies to advance the Chinese Communist Party’s military and economic agenda. Also in 2022, Schumer joined bipartisan colleagues to push the Biden administration to stop Apple from a previous consideration of integrating Chinese-made chips into their supply chain. For years, Schumer has also been actively pushing to add CXMT to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, which already includes YMTC after Schumer’s advocacy. Schumer is also co-lead of the bipartisan Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act , which would modernize U.S. export controls to ensure adversaries cannot buy "chokepoint" semiconductor manufacturing equipment (SME) technology from the United States or our partners. Among many actions, this bill would place tighter restrictions on all fabs run by CXMT, YMTC, and other Chinese firms of concern, cutting off access to critical semiconductor manufacturing tools. Schumer is actively working to include the MATCH Act in this year’s NDAA bill. Schumer and colleagues' letter to Apple can be found HERE or below: Dear Mr. Cook: We write to express our concern regarding credible reports that Apple has begun testing DRAM from ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) for potential use in devices and is allegedly lobbying U.S. federal officials against national security controls to permit the broader use of Chinese memory chips in Apple products. This short-sighted move would be a mistake, and it would ensure the world's most valuable consumer-electronics company grows dependent on critical supplies from a firm the United States government has formally designated as a Chinese military company. We urge Apple to abandon any effort to incorporate memory from CXMT, Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. (YMTC), or any other Chinese state-backed supplier into any of its products. The U.S. government has been clear that both CXMT and YMTC present significant national security threats. The Department of Defense designated both CXMT and YMTC as Chinese military companies under Section 1260H, and both remain on the list the Department updated last month. The Bureau of Industry and Security identified YMTC as a national security threat when it added the company to the Entity List in 2022. State-owned shareholders held over 35 percent of CXMT before its planned Shanghai listing, and CXMT moved into profit only after the global memory chip shortage took hold, after it ran heavy losses in earlier years that were sustained by state capital. Beijing has run this same playbook in countless critical supply chains before including steel, batteries, and shipbuilding, where state-subsidized capacity drove prices below market levels, forced trusted Western producers out of business, and made buyers dependent on America’s chief adversary for vital goods. Congress has also weighed in on the national security risks posed by CXMT and YMTC. Section 5949 of the FY 2023 NDAA barred federal agencies from acquiring products that use CXMT and YMTC semiconductors beginning in December 2027. If Apple pursues Chinese memory chips in its devices, it would be directly supporting a supply chain the U.S. government is legally bound to phase out of its devices. As the most demanding component buyer in the world, a decision by Apple to procure Chinese memory chips would carry weight well beyond the company’s own purchase orders. This validation would function as a signal that other buyers follow. That signal would arrive just as workers in Indiana, Idaho, New York, and Virginia carry out the largest expansion of domestic memory production in a generation, including the advanced packaging plant SK Hynix is building alongside Purdue University in West Lafayette, Indiana. Analysis indicates that CXMT’s pricing is currently, in some cases, higher than that of global competitors, and CXMT has recently hiked prices on its existing customers. Even if Apple were able to negotiate lower initial pricing from CXMT, this does not justify the national security exposure that Apple would create by qualifying or integrating chips from a designated Chinese military supplier into its products. That exposure should weigh far more heavily on the company than any short-lived savings a supply arrangement might promise. The limitation that CXMT memory would, for the moment, be confined to devices sold in China cannot be expected to hold, because once a part clears qualification for Apple production, extending it worldwide is a single procurement decision away. The revenue and reputational gains enjoyed by CXMT would hold regardless of where the finished device is eventually sold. Apple confronted a version of this very choice in 2022, when it evaluated YMTC NAND for the iPhone and, after congressional scrutiny, thought better of it. Accordingly, we request your responses to the following by August 21, 2026: Will Apple commit that it will not incorporate CXMT or YMTC memory into any Apple product, whether sold in the United States or abroad? If not, please explain why. Please describe the current status of Apple's testing or qualification of memory from CXMT, YMTC, and any other Chinese supplier, including which product lines and memory types, whether DRAM, NAND, or HBM, are involved. What information about Apple's products, technical specifications, or product roadmaps has Apple shared, or would it share, with CXMT, YMTC, or their representatives in the course of qualification? Has Apple assessed whether memory from CXMT or YMTC relies on the intellectual property of United States or allied memory manufacturers, including whether those Chinese suppliers are licensed to the relevant patents, and what legal or supply exposure that would create for Apple's products? Under a hypothetical procurement agreement, what access, if any, would CXMT, YMTC, or their personnel have to Apple's design, production, or supplier-management facilities in connection with this memory, and what data would that memory or those personnel be able to collect? During the current shortage, has Apple asked any United States or allied memory manufacturer for additional supply, increased allocation, or priority over other customers, and what was the result? Has Apple conducted any analysis of the supply chain security risks associated with sourcing memory from CXMT, YMTC, or other Chinese suppliers, including the risk of dependency on supply that could be restricted, controlled, disrupted, or terminated by the Chinese Communist Party or the Government of the People’s Republic of China? If so, please describe that analysis and its conclusions. The precedent Apple would set by addressing the memory shortage this way would shape the memory market and this country's security for years after supply has returned to normal, and we urge you to weigh that carefully before the company commits itself any further. We look forward to your response. ###

As Congress works on the upcoming Farm Bill, Schumer is urging New York House Republicans to work with Democrats to meet the needs of families suffering from the skyrocketing cost of living and stand with local elected officials, food banks, and families against these cuts. “85,000 New York families, kids, and seniors across the Southern Tier depend on SNAP to put food on the table. In April, Upstate New York Farms Suffered Crop Loss After Frost Damaged Early Growth Of Fruits And Vegetables – With Farmers Losing Anywhere From 15 To 100 Percent Of Their Crops Following Sustained Advocacy, Schumer, Gillibrand, And Ryan Deliver The Federal Resources Upstate New York Farmers Need To Recover And Get Ready For The Next Growing Season Schumer, Gillibrand, Ryan: Fed Relief On The Way To Help Upstate NY’s Farmers! After calling on the USDA to provide relief for New York farmers suffering losses following a devastating frost in April, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, and U.S. Congressman Pat Ryan today announced U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins heeded their call and has approved federal aid for New York fruit and specialty crop growers. The New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets estimates more than $30 million in losses to date, with apple, grape, stone fruit, onion, and other specialty crop growers potentially losing anywhere from 15 to 100 percent of their crops to the frost. “Upstate farmers work hard every season to put food on our tables and keep New York’s agricultural economy growing. When April weather severely damaged crops just as they were beginning to bloom, I stood up for the farmers who were hit hardest and fought to make sure they had the federal support they needed to recover. I’m proud to announce that USDA Secretary Rollins has heeded my call to help our farmers and is making critical resources available to growers, from the vineyards of the Finger Lakes to the orchards of the Capital Region ,” said Senator Schumer. “I encourage farmers in impacted counties to get the assistance they need to weather this tough season and lay the groundwork for a stronger harvest next year. I’ll always stand up for Upstate farmers and fight to ensure they have the resources they need to recover, keep growing, and protect New York’s economy.” “I am pleased that New York State’s request for a Secretarial disaster designation has been granted,” said Senator Gillibrand. “I fought to secure this approval and bring home the federal resources our farmers and growers urgently needed following the loss of their crops in the devastating April frost. Now, growers in affected regions across the state can access low-interest USDA loans to help them recover. I will always fight for New York’s farmers, and I look forward to seeing these federal dollars at work to bring them the relief they need and deserve.” “The freeze this spring was absolutely devastating to our farmers and growers in the Hudson Valley. Many of our apple growers told me they lost nearly 100% of their crop. Hearing and seeing the damage firsthand made it crystal clear we needed urgent action from the USDA,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “For months, I’ve been pushing at every level to help secure this official Disaster Designation, which will now unlock millions of dollars in emergency loans and resources to help our farmers and growers begin to recover. I’m grateful for the USDA’s action, but this is just the first step. I’ll be ready to help all those who were impacted by the frost apply for and get access to this assistance, so their businesses can continue to thrive in the Hudson Valley.” The lawmakers last month sent a letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins urging her to approve a Secretarial Disaster Designation, allowing affected farmers to apply for USDA low-interest emergency loans. The counties the lawmakers called for relief for included in the Disaster Designation are the primary counties of Albany, Columbia, Dutchess, Erie, Greene, Niagara, Chautauqua, Onondaga, Orange, Putnam, Schuyler, Sullivan, Ulster, Westchester, and Yates Counties, and the contiguous counties of Cayuga, Chemung, Cortland, Delaware, Erie, Madison, Monroe, Ontario, Orleans, Oswego, Rensselaer, Rockland, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Seneca, Steuben, Tompkins, and Wayne Counties. The letter was also signed by Reps. Paul Tonko (D-NY-20), Josh Riley (D-NY-19), and Tim Kennedy (D-NY-26). The full text of the letter can be found here . According to USDA’s 2022 Census of Agriculture, New York is one of the top-ranking specialty crop states in the country, including second in apples and third in grapes. Many specialty crop farms also support New York’s agritourism and economy through pick-your-own operations and value-added products, such as hard cider and wine. ###

As ICE Refuses To Be Transparent On Its Plans For Orange County, Senators Say Enough Is Enough, Stop The Secrecy, Work With Local Leaders, And Give Assurances There Will Be No ICE Facility In Orange County Earlier This Year, After Community-Wide And Bipartisan Opposition, ICE Backed Off Plans To Convert Another Orange County Warehouse – In Chester – Into An ICE Mass Detention Facility – After Schumer Sounded The Alarm With Local Leaders And Community Members Schumer, Gillibrand: No ICE Facility In Newburgh Amid confusion and broad community concern surrounding ICE leasing an abandoned warehouse in Newburgh , U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand today demanded answers about the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) plans for Orange County. Earlier this month, new publicly available records revealed that ICE leased a warehouse near Stewart International Airport, prompting broad, bipartisan concern among local residents, elected officials, and community members. Due to a lack of transparency surrounding the facility’s intended use, the senators demanded answers from ICE about its plans for the site and made it clear that the community must be kept informed about future developments. “Since day one, DHS management in the Hudson Valley has been secretive about its plans and dismissive of the local region’s concerns. After weeks of confusion and ultimately backing off plans for a facility in Chester, ICE is now quietly trying to build a detention center in Newburgh, which is opposed by a broad cross-section of the region,” said Senator Schumer. “Local leaders and community members can’t get a straight answer on what ICE is planning, and that is just not acceptable. There is deep and bipartisan opposition to ICE’s plan. That’s why Senator Gillibrand and I are demanding concrete answers on what the facility will be used for and assurances that no plan will move forward without the community’s support. I have said it before, and I will say it again: there should be no ICE mass detention center in Orange County, not in Newburgh, not in Chester, not anywhere.” “GSA and ICE officials have been withholding information about the development of this proposed facility and the effects that it will have on the local community in Newburgh,” said Senator Gillibrand. “This is unacceptable, and disregards the overwhelming opposition from locals to the creation of an immigration detention facility in Newburgh. Senator Schumer and I will not back down until ICE gives us the answers we need and assures us that it will heed the concerns of all residents going forward. We will not stand for the continued unjust actions of ICE in our communities in New York and across the country.” Last month, the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) awarded a $35.5 million, 15-year lease to a Texas-based contractor. GSA documents showed it was looking for a space for “detainee buses and vans” and 24/7 government access near Stewart International Airport. ICE has still not communicated with the Hudson Valley community about its plans for the facility. Schumer and Gillibrand have both vehemently opposed proposed plans to build an immigrant detention center in Newburgh and are now demanding concrete and detailed answers regarding ICE’s plan. Local leaders, both Democrat and Republican, have overwhelmingly opposed the plan. The Town of Newburgh unanimously approved a resolution opposing an ICE detention center, and hundreds of Hudson Valley residents have spoken out against this plan. In February, Schumer demanded answers and an investigation into ICE’s disastrous management and unacceptable lack of transparency in Orange County after weeks of chaos, secrecy, and changing stories surrounding ICE’s plans for a mass detention facility in Chester. Ultimately, ICE announced there were no plans to convert the warehouse in Chester into a large-scale immigration detention center. The senators said this new lease is part of an alarming pattern of ICE purchasing warehouses without coordination with the local communities, fueling concerns that these facilities could ultimately be converted into detention centers. Senator Schumer has led congressional efforts to strengthen oversight of ICE and advance reforms aimed at increasing transparency and accountability in immigration enforcement. Alongside his colleagues, he has called for commonsense guardrails, including prohibiting enforcement actions at sensitive locations such as schools and courthouses, requiring officers to display identification, banning the use of masks during enforcement operations, preventing racial profiling, mandating the use of body-worn cameras, ensuring access to counsel for individuals in detention facilities, and improving oversight and coordination with state and local authorities. Schumer has argued that federal immigration agents cannot continue to operate in communities without accountability and that Congress must act to protect constitutional rights while promoting fair and effective immigration enforcement. Schumer and Gillibrand’s letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and GSA Administrator Edward Forst can be found HERE or below: Dear Secretary Mullin and Administrator Forst: We write to get clarity and demand answers into the recent $35.5 million, 15-year lease purchase of a 42,377-square-foot industrial warehouse located at 800 Corporate Blvd, Newburgh, NY 12550, for U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations. This purchase has generated significant concern among local residents, elected officials, and community stakeholders due to the lack of transparency surrounding the facility's intended use. Although U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) and ICE have publicly identified the tenant agencies and developer, they have provided few details about the operations that will take place at the site or the potential impacts on the surrounding community. These concerns are reinforced by GSA’s initial 2025 Request for Lease Proposals (RLP) Summary, which outlined requirements that go beyond a typical federal office lease and suggest a facility designed to support secure law enforcement operations. The RLP called for a dedicated sally port to accommodate "detainee buses and vans," a location away from residential areas, schools, religious institutions, and retail centers, as well as 24/7 access, an emergency generator, secured parking, and enhanced security features. Together, these specialized requirements indicate a facility intended for more than routine administrative office use. Without clear information from GSA and ICE, the community has been left to interpret these requirements on its own, making it difficult for residents and local leaders to meaningfully assess the potential impacts of the proposed facility or engage in an informed public discussion about the project. This lack of transparency has alarmed leaders and stakeholders at every level, creating unease among those who are expected to deal with the reality of any upscaling of DHS and ICE operations in their communities. This community has faced a similar proposal before in Chester, New York, and has been unequivocal and bipartisan in expressing its opposition to immigration detention activities within the area. That experience demonstrated the community's clear and consistent position: residents and local leaders do not support the establishment or expansion of immigration detention operations in their community. Given this recent history, any purchase that raises similar concerns warrants meaningful transparency and engagement from federal agencies so that the public is fully informed about the intended use of the facility and its potential impact on the surrounding community. To address these unanswered questions surrounding purchase, development, and potential impact on the surrounding community, we request responses to the following questions on the intended use of this facility located at 800 Corporate Blvd Newburgh, NY 12550: What is the intended use of the facility located at 800 Corporate Boulevard in Newburgh, New York, and what operations will DHS and ICE conduct at this site? Please list every DHS component, contractor and program expected to use the property. What is the expected timeline for the facility becoming operational, and what steps remain before DHS and ICE begin using the site? Please identify any remaining approvals, construction, tenant improvements, permits or other conditions that must be completed before occupancy. Please provide the lease, occupancy agreement, solicitation, program of requirements, statement of work, improvement plans, security requirements, and all associated contracts and subcontracts. Please identify the lessor and beneficial owners, all operating contractors, the appropriations accounts funding the lease and operations, the annual rent and improvement costs, and the total estimated lifecycle costs. Who approved the project, when was it approved and what operational needs is it intended to address? Is the project aimed at increasing detention capacity in New York, supporting increased enforcement operations in New York, expanding the operations of ICE Air, or supporting a broader regional deportation plan? Will the facility be used for the detention, temporary holding, processing, transportation, or transfer of individuals in federal custody?
